white-forest.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Elzette into Diabell, Queen

One Elzette becomes three Level 8s that protect each other. Elzette finds Silvy, Silvy finds the Field Spell Witch, and Witch finds a second Level 2. Silvy + that Level 2 make the Synchro Tuner Rciela, and Rciela + Elzette make the Queen. Along the way Rciela and Elzette Azamina fetch the Diabell cards, so Diabellze and Diabellstar Vengeance join for free.

Starting hand: Elzette of the White Forest, Forbidden Droplet · Normal Summon: Silvy of the White Forest

  1. Send a spare Spell/Trap (here Forbidden Droplet) from your hand to the GY to Special Summon Elzette. She adds Silvy from your Deck.
  2. Normal Summon Silvy. She adds Witch of the White Forest from your Deck.
  3. Activate Witch. It adds Elzette, Azamina from your Deck. From now on, no DARK monsters from your Extra Deck this turn.
  4. Reveal Elzette, Azamina in your hand: she Special Summons herself.
  5. Synchro Summon Rciela (Level 6) using Silvy (4, Tuner) + Elzette, Azamina (2). Azamina, used as Synchro Material, adds Sinful Spoils of Subversion - Snake-Eye.
  6. Rciela was Summoned: send Witch from your Field Zone to the GY and add Diabellze (she counts as a White Forest card).
  7. Send Snake-Eye from your hand to Special Summon Diabellze. Her Summon effect sends Curse of Diabell from your Deck to the GY.
  8. Curse of Diabell was sent from the Deck, so it adds Filia Diabell.
  9. Synchro Summon Diabell, Queen (Level 8) using Rciela (6, Tuner Synchro) + Elzette (2). Because a Tuner Synchro was used, she returns Witch from your GY to your hand.
  10. Activate Filia Diabell: add Diabellstar Vengeance.
  11. Banish Filia Diabell (Spell) and Curse of Diabell (Trap) from your GY to Special Summon Diabellstar Vengeance. Filia was banished, so your Diabell monsters gain 500 ATK.

End board: Diabell, Queen + Diabellze + Diabellstar Vengeance, with Witch in hand. With 2+ Diabell monsters, Diabellze stops their effects destroying your monsters. When they activate something, the Queen sends Witch from your hand to Summon Silvera, which flips all their face-up monsters face-down (and Elzette returns from your GY to your hand). Vengeance pays half your LP to destroy 1 of their cards.

  • Each White Forest effect is once per turn by name: a second Elzette can't use her Summon effect the same turn.
  • If Ash Blossom stops Silvy's search, still make Rciela with a Level 2 and use Rciela's search to get Witch.
  • The Queen only returns a Spell/Trap if a Tuner Synchro (Rciela, Silvera or Poplar) was used as her material.
Line B — Diabellstar into Vengeance

The line for hands without Elzette or Silvy, and it uses no Normal Summon. WANTED finds Diabellstar, who Summons herself by sending 1 card and Sets a Trap from your Deck. Diabellze sends that Trap to Summon herself, then puts Diabellstar Vengeance in the GY, and Vengeance Summons itself from there. Three witches protect each other, and Vengeance destroys a card on their turn.

Starting hand: WANTED: Seeker of Sinful Spoils, Diabellze the White Witch, Forbidden Droplet · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate WANTED: add Diabellstar the Black Witch from your Deck.
  2. Send Forbidden Droplet (any card works) from your hand to the GY to Special Summon Diabellstar.
  3. Diabellstar was Summoned: Set Sinful Spoils of Slumber - Morrian from your Deck.
  4. Send the Set Morrian from your field to the GY to Special Summon Diabellze from your hand.
  5. Diabellze was Summoned: send Diabellstar Vengeance from your Deck to the GY (it always counts as a Sinful Spoils card).
  6. Banish Forbidden Droplet (Spell) and Morrian (Trap) from your GY to Special Summon Vengeance from the GY.
  7. Banish WANTED from your GY: put the banished Morrian on the bottom of your Deck and draw 1.

End board: Diabellstar the Black Witch + Diabellze + Diabellstar Vengeance. Diabellze stops their effects destroying your monsters. On their turn Vengeance pays half your LP to destroy 1 of their cards, then (with another Diabell on the field) Summons Silvera, Rciela or Poplar from your Extra Deck.

  • Vengeance needs exactly 1 Spell and 1 Trap to banish. Plan which Trap reaches your hand or GY (Morrian or Curse of Diabell).
  • If Diabellze's send effect is negated, Vengeance never reaches the GY and you end on two monsters.
  • If you also hold Elzette, play this line first and use the Set Sinful Spoils card as her cost.
Going second — Super Polymerization

Super Polymerization is a Quick-Play Spell: discard 1 card, then Fusion Summon using monsters from either field. Neither player can respond to it. Two of their best monsters (or one of theirs and one of yours) become one Fusion Monster on your side. The materials are sent to the GY without being targeted or destroyed, so their protection doesn't help. Pick the Fusion by what the two monsters share:

  • Same Type and same Attribute: Garura, Wings of Resonant Life. Any 2 monsters with different names. Garura doubles the battle damage it deals and draws you 1 card when it goes to the GY. Your own pair: Elzette + Silvy (LIGHT Spellcasters).
  • Same Attribute, different Types: Mudragon of the Swamp. Your opponent can't target Mudragon, or any monster sharing its Attribute, with card effects. Your own pair: Elzette (Spellcaster) + Diabellze (Illusion), both LIGHT.
  • Two DARK monsters (no Tokens): Starving Venom Fusion Dragon. Gains the ATK of one of their Special Summoned monsters this turn, and can copy the name and effects of a Level 5+ monster they control.
  • Same Type, different Attributes: Favorite HERO Flame Wingman. Gains 1000 ATK when it battles a monster with 2200+ ATK, and can Fusion Summon again after a monster is destroyed by battle.
  • You choose the Fusion when Super Polymerization resolves, so check each monster's Type and Attribute before you activate it.
  • Witch of the White Forest's lock blocks Garura and Starving Venom (both DARK). Use Super Polymerization before you activate Witch.
  • You can also Set it and activate it on your opponent's turn, in the middle of their combo.
white-forest.str:
• Two engines that each start from one card, and one of them needs no Normal Summon.
  • The Queen and Poplar Summon Synchros on the opponent's turn, so your disruption is hard to predict.
  • Removal that doesn't destroy: Silvera flips monsters face-down, and Snake-Eye turns them into Continuous Spells.
  • A full going-second package: Mulcharmy Fuwalos, Forbidden Droplet and Super Polymerization.
white-forest.weak:
• Every play costs a Spell/Trap, so hands with few of them stall.
  • Witch's DARK lock removes five Extra Deck options on the turn you search with it.
  • Mulcharmy Fuwalos is dead once you have a card on the field.

horus-mitsurugi.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Walls into Imsety + Hapi

The Horus engine from one Field Spell and two spare cards, with no Normal Summon. Walls finds Imsety. Imsety sends itself to the GY to find the real King's Sarcophagus, and Sarcophagus sends Hapi from the Deck. Both then Summon themselves from the GY, because you control King's Sarcophagus.

Starting hand: Walls of the Imperial Tomb, Droll & Lock Bird, Nibiru, the Primal Being · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate Walls of the Imperial Tomb in your Field Zone. While it is there, its name is King's Sarcophagus.
  2. Walls' effect: add Imsety from your Deck, then put 1 card from your hand (here Nibiru) on the bottom of your Deck.
  3. Imsety's effect: send Imsety and 1 other card (here Droll & Lock Bird) from your hand to the GY. Add King's Sarcophagus, then draw 1.
  4. You control "King's Sarcophagus" (Walls), so Special Summon Imsety from your GY.
  5. Activate King's Sarcophagus. Send the card you drew from your hand to the GY, then send Hapi from your Deck to the GY.
  6. Special Summon Hapi from your GY the same way.

End board: Imsety + Hapi with both Sarcophagus cards. Effects that destroy without targeting can't destroy them. If their effect removes one of your other cards, Imsety sends 1 card on the field to the GY and Hapi returns 2 cards from the GYs or banishment. If they are destroyed anyway, they Summon themselves again next turn.

  • Opening Imsety and no Walls? Start at step 3, then activate King's Sarcophagus and continue.
  • Imsety and Hapi can each Summon themselves from the GY once per turn.
  • King's Sarcophagus's send effect costs 1 card from your hand each time. A second Imsety in hand is a good card to send.
Line B — Mitsurugi Ritual into Murakumo and Futsu

Two Spells become both Ritual bosses and a Set negate. Mitsurugi Ritual pays for Murakumo by Tributing two Level 4s from your Deck, and each one searches because it was Tributed. Mitsurugi Mirror then Tributes Murakumo to Summon Futsu, and Murakumo searches and comes straight back.

Starting hand: Mitsurugi Prayers, Mitsurugi Ritual · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate Mitsurugi Prayers without Tributing: add Ame no Murakumo from your Deck.
  2. Activate Mitsurugi Ritual, second effect: Ritual Summon Murakumo from your hand by Tributing Aramasa + Saji (Level 4 + 4) from your Deck.
  3. Murakumo was Special Summoned: destroy all monsters your opponent controls (this is your board wipe when going second).
  4. Aramasa was Tributed: add Futsu no Mitama. Saji was Tributed: add Mitsurugi Mirror.
  5. Activate Mitsurugi Mirror: Ritual Summon Futsu from your hand by Tributing Murakumo (Level 8) from your field.
  6. Murakumo was Tributed: add Mitsurugi Great Purification, then Murakumo Special Summons itself.
  7. Set Mitsurugi Great Purification. You still have your Normal Summon.

End board: Murakumo + Futsu with Great Purification Set. Each turn, the first time they activate something, Murakumo makes them discard 1 card or it is negated. When they Special Summon, Futsu revives Aramasa or Saji, which searches again. Great Purification Tributes Futsu to negate and destroy, and Futsu adds a card and returns.

  • Mitsurugi Ritual has two effects, each once per turn. Only the one that Summons from your hand can Tribute from the Deck.
  • Each Murakumo effect is once per turn, so it doesn't wipe their field again when it comes back in step 6.
  • Only 1 Mitsurugi Prayers per turn. With a Mikoto in hand, Tribute it on activation to get both of Prayers' effects.
Line C — Rank 8 finish with Numeron Dragon

What to do with Imsety + Hapi once your Ritual plays are done. Two Level 8s make Number 97: Draglubion. Draglubion pulls Numeron Dragon out of the Extra Deck, and Numeron Dragon gains 1000 ATK for every Rank on the field: 9000. After Murakumo has destroyed their monsters, that is a winning direct attack.

Starting hand: Walls of the Imperial Tomb, Droll & Lock Bird, Nibiru, the Primal Being · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Play Line A to put Imsety + Hapi on the field. If you have Mitsurugi plays, make them first.
  2. Xyz Summon Number 97: Draglubion (Rank 8) using Imsety + Hapi. Your opponent can't target it.
  3. Detach 1 material: take Numeron Dragon and Titanic Galaxy from your Extra Deck. Special Summon Numeron Dragon and attach Titanic Galaxy to it.
  4. Numeron Dragon detaches its material: it gains 1000 ATK × the Ranks on the field (1 + 8), so 9000 ATK until the end of their next turn.
  5. Attack with Numeron Dragon. Directly it deals 9000. Into an Attack Position monster it deals 9000 minus that monster's ATK.

End board: Going second this ends the game. Going first, Summon Titanic Galaxy with Draglubion instead and attach Numeron Dragon: Titanic Galaxy negates one Spell effect activated on the field each turn, and Draglubion is a 3000 ATK monster they can't target.

  • After Draglubion's effect you can't Special Summon other monsters this turn, and only the monster it Summoned can attack.
  • Number 84: Pain Gainer is the other option: Xyz Summon it on top of Draglubion (before using Draglubion's effect), then detach to destroy every face-up monster with 2200 or less DEF.
  • Xyz Summoning uses up Imsety and Hapi, so going first you can also just keep them.
Going second — Super Polymerization

Super Polymerization is a Quick-Play Spell: discard 1 card, then Fusion Summon using monsters from either field. Neither player can respond to it. Two of their best monsters (or one of theirs and one of yours) become one Fusion Monster on your side. The materials are sent to the GY without being targeted or destroyed, so their protection doesn't help. Pick the Fusion by what the two monsters share:

  • Two DARK monsters (no Tokens): Starving Venom Fusion Dragon. Gains the ATK of one of their Special Summoned monsters this turn, and can copy the name and effects of a Level 5+ monster they control. Your own pair: any Horus or Mitsurugi monster. Every one except Hapi is DARK, so one of yours plus one DARK monster of theirs works.
  • Same Type and same Attribute: Garura, Wings of Resonant Life. Any 2 monsters with different names. Garura doubles the battle damage it deals and draws you 1 card when it goes to the GY. Your own pair: Aramasa + Saji (DARK Reptiles).
  • Same Attribute, different Types: Mudragon of the Swamp. Your opponent can't target Mudragon, or any monster sharing its Attribute, with card effects. Your own pair: Imsety (Spellcaster) + a Mitsurugi (Reptile), both DARK.
  • Same Type, different Attributes: Favorite HERO Flame Wingman. Gains 1000 ATK when it battles a monster with 2200+ ATK, and can Fusion Summon again after a monster is destroyed by battle.
  • You choose the Fusion when Super Polymerization resolves, so check each monster's Type and Attribute before you activate it.
  • The card you discard is a cost. A Horus monster is the best discard, because it can Summon itself from the GY.
  • You can also Set it and activate it on your opponent's turn, in the middle of their combo.
horus-mitsurugi.str:
• Two engines that both make Level 8 monsters, and neither needs the other.
  • Murakumo destroys every monster they control just by arriving.
  • Horus monsters return from the GY every turn for free.
  • Great Purification is a searchable negate whose cost pays itself back.

  • The Horus half stops if both King's Sarcophagus cards are removed.
  • Only 1 copy of each Mikoto, so a banished one is missed.
  • Draglubion's effect ends your Special Summons for the turn.

kashtira-maliss.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Dormouse into Hearts Crypter

One Normal Summon becomes two Link-3s. Dormouse banishes White Rabbit, and both keep Summoning themselves back while Haggard Lizardose and Red Ransom are built from them. Red Ransom finds Underground for a third monster. The Trap TB-11 then banishes Red Ransom as a cost, and Red Ransom simply returns, bringing March Hare with it.

Starting hand: Maliss <P> Dormouse · Normal Summon: Maliss <P> Dormouse

  1. Normal Summon Dormouse. Its effect banishes White Rabbit from your Deck.
  2. White Rabbit was banished: pay 300 LP to Special Summon it. When Summoned, it Sets TB-11 from your Deck.
  3. Link Summon Haggard Lizardose using Dormouse + White Rabbit.
  4. Lizardose's effect: banish Dormouse from your GY (target Lizardose). Dormouse was banished: pay 300 LP to Special Summon it.
  5. Link Summon Red Ransom using Lizardose + Dormouse. It adds Maliss in Underground from your Deck.
  6. Activate Underground: banish Chessy Cat from your Deck. Chessy Cat was banished: pay 300 LP to Special Summon it.
  7. Activate the Set TB-11 by banishing Red Ransom from your field. TB-11 Special Summons a second Chessy Cat from your Deck.
  8. Red Ransom was banished: pay 900 LP to Special Summon it, then banish March Hare from your Deck.
  9. March Hare was banished: pay 300 LP, target March Hare itself, and add it to your hand.
  10. March Hare's effect in hand: banish TB-11 from your GY to Special Summon March Hare.
  11. Link Summon Hearts Crypter using both Chessy Cats + March Hare, to the Extra Monster Zone, so that it points to Red Ransom.

End board: Hearts Crypter + Red Ransom + Maliss in Underground, and you still hold your other 4 cards. On either turn Hearts Crypter shuffles the banished TB-11 into your Deck to banish 1 card on the field, and that can't be negated. With Underground, their monsters can only attack your Maliss Links. You paid 2100 LP.

  • Cynet Mining (add Dormouse), Gold Sarcophagus or Maliss in Underground (banish Dormouse from the Deck) start the same line. The last two keep your Normal Summon.
  • Put Red Ransom in a Main Monster Zone diagonally below the Extra Monster Zone when it returns in step 8. Hearts Crypter must point to a monster for its effect to be un-negatable.
  • Hearts Crypter needs a banished Maliss card each time. Here that is TB-11, then any Maliss monster you banish later.
Line B — Kashtira first (going second)

Fenrir and Unicorn only Summon themselves while you control no monsters, so they are always your first play. Wraitsoth finds Fenrir, Fenrir finds Unicorn for next turn, and you still have your Normal Summon and the whole Maliss line. In the Battle Phase Fenrir banishes one of their cards face-down.

Starting hand: Pressured Planet Wraitsoth, Maliss <P> Dormouse · Normal Summon: Maliss <P> Dormouse

  1. Activate Pressured Planet Wraitsoth: add Kashtira Fenrir from your Deck.
  2. You control no monsters: Special Summon Fenrir from your hand.
  3. Fenrir's effect: add Kashtira Unicorn from your Deck. Keep it for a turn when your field is empty again.
  4. Normal Summon Dormouse and play Line A. Fenrir has no Extra Deck lock, so every Link is available.
  5. Fenrir declares an attack: banish 1 face-up card they control, face-down. Then attack with everything.

End board: Fenrir beside your Maliss Links, with Unicorn in hand. On their turn, the first monster effect they activate lets Fenrir banish another face-up card face-down.

  • Line A step 6 replaces Wraitsoth with Maliss in Underground in the Field Zone. Wraitsoth has already searched, so nothing is lost.
  • Fenrir's search and its banish are each once per turn.
  • If they have a monster, a Bystial can also come first: it banishes a LIGHT or DARK monster from their GY as a Quick Effect.
Line C — Accesscode Talker finish

The going-second ending to Line A. Stop after Underground brings out Chessy Cat, and Link Red Ransom + Chessy Cat into Accesscode Talker. It gains 3000 ATK, then banishes Links from your GY to destroy a card each. They can't respond. Red Ransom is one of the Links you banish, so it Summons itself again and attacks too.

Starting hand: Maliss <P> Dormouse · Normal Summon: Maliss <P> Dormouse

  1. Play Line A steps 1–6: you control Red Ransom + Chessy Cat, with Haggard Lizardose in your GY.
  2. Link Summon Accesscode Talker using Red Ransom + Chessy Cat. Target Red Ransom: Accesscode gains 3000 ATK (5300).
  3. Accesscode's effect: banish Lizardose (WATER) from your GY and destroy 1 card they control.
  4. Use it again: banish Red Ransom (DARK) from your GY and destroy a second card.
  5. Red Ransom was banished: pay 900 LP to Special Summon it, then banish March Hare from your Deck, which adds itself to your hand.
  6. Attack. Accesscode has 5300 ATK and Red Ransom has 2900 (Dormouse gave Maliss monsters +600 this turn): 8200 damage on an empty field.

End board: Two of their cards destroyed with no chance to respond, then 8200 damage from Accesscode Talker and Red Ransom. If they survive, the Set TB-11 and the March Hare in your hand restart the engine next turn.

  • Accesscode can't banish two Links of the same Attribute in one turn. Lizardose is WATER and Red Ransom is DARK, so you get exactly two destroys.
  • Dormouse's +600 ATK applies to Maliss monsters only, not to Accesscode Talker.
  • You paid 1800 LP on this line. Check that their remaining cards can't punish that.
kashtira-maliss.str:
• One Maliss monster is a full combo, and nine other cards find one.
  • Hearts Crypter's banish can't be negated while it points to a monster.
  • Kashtira gives a strong play that doesn't use the Normal Summon or the Maliss engine.
  • 22 hand traps and going-second cards.

• A full combo costs about 2000 LP.
  • White Rabbit and Dormouse are 1 copy each (both Limited).
  • Maliss in Underground and Pressured Planet Wraitsoth share the Field Zone.
  • Cards that stop banishing or banished effects shut the engine off.

runick-typhoon.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Plan A — Boarder, Fountain and Allure (going first)

Turn one is set-up. Inspector Boarder goes down first because it needs an empty field. Tip finds Fountain. A second Runick Spell is used in Summon mode for Munin, who finds Allure, and Fountain turns the used Tip into a new card. You keep your answers in hand for their turn.

Starting hand: Inspector Boarder, Runick Tip, Runick Slumber, Runick Flashing Fire, Runick Freezing Curses · Normal Summon: Inspector Boarder

  1. Normal Summon Inspector Boarder while you control no monsters.
  2. Activate Runick Tip, first effect: add Runick Fountain and banish the top card of their Deck.
  3. Activate Runick Fountain in your Field Zone.
  4. Activate Runick Slumber, second effect: Special Summon Munin to the Extra Monster Zone.
  5. You activated a Runick Quick-Play, so Fountain triggers: put Tip from your GY on the bottom of your Deck and draw 1.
  6. Munin was Summoned: discard the card you need least and add Runick Allure. Activate it.

End board: Boarder + Munin + Fountain + Allure, with Flashing Fire and Freezing Curses in hand. On their turn: Flashing Fire destroys a Special Summoned monster, Freezing Curses negates a monster, Allure banishes 1 extra card each time, and Fountain puts the used Spells back to draw up to 3.

  • No Tip? Use any Runick Spell's Summon mode for Hugin instead: discard 1 and it adds Fountain.
  • With Boarder and Munin (a Fusion) on the field, each player gets 1 monster effect per turn. Munin's search uses yours.
  • If they target Fountain or Allure, banish Munin to negate that effect and destroy the card.
Their turn — Which Runick Spell answers what

With Runick Fountain on the field you activate these from your hand during the opponent's turn. Use each one on the card it is best against, then let Fountain return up to 3 of them to your Deck and draw that many. Each name can be activated once per turn.

  • They Special Summon a key monster: Runick Flashing Fire. Destroy it. Banishes the top 2 cards of their Deck.
  • A monster on the field activates an effect: Runick Freezing Curses. Chain it to negate that monster's effects for the turn. Banishes 3.
  • They Set or activate a Spell/Trap that stays on the field: Runick Destruction. Destroy it. Banishes 4.
  • They try to destroy Boarder or attack over it: Runick Slumber. Target your own monster: the next time it would be destroyed this turn, it isn't. Banishes 3.
  • They search a card: Runick Dispelling. Discards 1 random card from their hand. Banishes 2.
  • Nothing to answer: Runick Golden Droplet, Runick Smiting Storm. Golden Droplet banishes 4 (they draw 1). Smiting Storm banishes 1 per card they control.
  • Runick Allure banishes 1 more card every time a Quick-Play Spell is activated.
  • Fountain's recycle is once per turn. It only targets Runick Quick-Plays already in your GY, so trigger it with your second or third Spell.
  • The second mode (Summon a Fusion) is still there on their turn: Hugin to protect Fountain, or Sleipnir to banish an attacker.
Plan B — Breaking a board (going second)

Going second you clear the field before you set up. Lightning Storm only works while you control no face-up cards, so it comes first. Then Boarder and Fountain go down, and each Quick-Play removes one more card while thinning their Deck.

Starting hand: Lightning Storm, Inspector Boarder, Runick Fountain, Runick Destruction, Forbidden Droplet, Runick Flashing Fire · Normal Summon: Inspector Boarder

  1. You control no face-up cards: activate Lightning Storm. Destroy all their Attack Position monsters, or all their Spells and Traps.
  2. Normal Summon Inspector Boarder while you control no monsters.
  3. Activate Runick Fountain.
  4. Activate Runick Destruction: destroy 1 Spell/Trap they control and banish the top 4 cards of their Deck.
  5. Activate Forbidden Droplet: send 1 other card from your hand or field to the GY to halve the ATK of 1 of their monsters and negate its effects.
  6. Activate Runick Flashing Fire: destroy 1 Special Summoned monster and banish 2. Fountain returns Destruction to your Deck and you draw 1.

End board: Inspector Boarder + Runick Fountain against a broken board, with their Deck 6 cards thinner. Boarder now limits what they can rebuild with, and you skip your next Battle Phase.

  • Harpie's Feather Duster does the Spell/Trap half of Lightning Storm with no condition.
  • Forbidden Droplet can't be responded to by the card types you sent as its cost.
  • Destruction, Droplet and Flashing Fire are all Quick-Plays: with Allure out, each banishes 1 more card.
Plan C — TY-PHON from one monster

Super Starslayer TY-PHON normally needs two Level 12 monsters. It has a shortcut: during the turn your opponent Special Summoned 2 or more monsters from the Extra Deck, or the turn after, you can Xyz Summon it using only your highest-ATK monster. It answers boards that single Runick Spells can't.

Starting hand: Inspector Boarder · Normal Summon: Inspector Boarder

  1. They Special Summon 2 or more monsters from the Extra Deck. You control Inspector Boarder or Freki (2000 ATK).
  2. On your turn, Xyz Summon TY-PHON using only your highest-ATK monster. You can't Normal or Special Summon for the rest of the turn.
  3. Detach the material: return 1 monster on the field to the hand. An Extra Deck monster goes back to the Extra Deck.

End board: TY-PHON (2900 ATK) with their best monster gone. While TY-PHON is on the field, neither player can activate the effects of monsters with 3000 or more ATK.

  • Using Inspector Boarder as the material gives up its lock. Use Freki when you have it.
  • The deck runs 3 TY-PHON because the Summon uses up the monster each time.
  • TY-PHON is an Xyz Monster, so with a Boarder still on the field it adds 1 monster-effect slot for each player.
runick-typhoon.str:
• Answers come from the hand on the opponent's turn, so there is little for them to remove first.
  • Fountain draws up to 3 cards a turn, so you don't run out.
  • Inspector Boarder and Dimensional Fissure shut down many decks by themselves.
  • Real going-second cards: Lightning Storm, Feather Duster, Droplet ×2, TY-PHON ×3.
runick-typhoon.weak:
• Almost everything depends on Runick Fountain staying on the field.
  • No Battle Phase most turns, so games are long and a stalled opponent can recover.
  • Inspector Boarder restricts your own Runick Fusions.
  • Each Runick Spell handles one card: a full board going second needs a breaker.

Line A — Mitsurugi before War Zone

The Ritual half, played first because War Zone would lock it out. Pre-Preparation finds Mirror and Murakumo, and Prayers finds a Level 4 to pay for it. Murakumo destroys every monster they control. Saji, Tributed, finds Mitsurugi Ritual, which Tributes Murakumo to bring Futsu from the Deck, and Murakumo comes straight back.

Starting hand: Pre-Preparation of Rites, Mitsurugi Prayers · Normal Summon: Mitsurugi no Mikoto, Aramasa

  1. Activate Pre-Preparation of Rites: add Mitsurugi Mirror and Murakumo from your Deck.
  2. Activate Mitsurugi Prayers without Tributing: add Aramasa.
  3. Normal Summon Aramasa. It adds Saji from your Deck.
  4. Activate Mirror: Ritual Summon Murakumo from your hand by Tributing Aramasa (field) + Saji (hand), Level 4 + 4.
  5. Murakumo was Special Summoned: destroy all monsters they control. Saji was Tributed: add Mitsurugi Ritual.
  6. Activate Mitsurugi Ritual, first effect: Ritual Summon Futsu from your Deck by Tributing Murakumo (Level 8).
  7. Murakumo was Tributed: add Great Purification, then Murakumo Special Summons itself. Set Great Purification.

End board: Murakumo + Futsu with Great Purification Set. When they activate something, Murakumo makes them discard 1 card or it is negated. When they Special Summon, Futsu revives Aramasa or Saji, which searches. Great Purification Tributes Futsu to negate and destroy, and Futsu returns.

  • Do this before Ryu-Ge War Zone, never after.
  • Aramasa already searched when it was Normal Summoned, so it doesn't search again when Tributed. Each Mikoto effect is once per turn.
  • Murakumo's wipe is once per turn: it doesn't destroy again when it returns.
Line B — Melody into Mistva and three Realms

The Ryu-Ge half from one Spell. Melody finds Mistva and Anva. Mistva, placed in a Pendulum Zone, finds War Zone and puts itself in the Extra Deck face-up. War Zone then Summons three Level 10s, Anva destroys one of them, and that destruction lets Mistva Summon itself and swap your cards for Realms.

Starting hand: The Melody of Awakening Dragon, Nibiru, the Primal Being · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate Melody: discard 1 card (here Nibiru) and add Anva and Mistva from your Deck.
  2. Place Mistva in a Pendulum Zone. Its effect adds Ryu-Ge War Zone, then Mistva destroys itself and goes to your Extra Deck face-up.
  3. Activate War Zone. Take Kaiva, Emva and Hakva from your Deck: Kaiva to your hand, Hakva banished, Emva to the GY.
  4. War Zone's effect: Special Summon 3 Ryu-Ge: a second Anva from your Deck, Emva from the GY and Hakva from banishment.
  5. Anva was Special Summoned: target Emva and destroy it.
  6. A monster was destroyed: Tribute Hakva to Special Summon Mistva from your Extra Deck (a Ritual Summon).
  7. Mistva's effect: destroy War Zone and Anva, then place Wyrm Winds and Sea Spires from your Deck.
  8. Anva was destroyed: place Dino Domains from your Deck.
  9. 2 or more cards were destroyed this turn: Special Summon Kaiva from your hand.

End board: Mistva (3800 ATK) + Kaiva (3300) + all three Realms, with an Anva still in hand. On their turn Mistva can negate a monster effect, return a card to the hand and make a monster's ATK 0. Each use puts one Realm on the bottom of your Deck. Kaiva can use the negate too.

  • Ryu-Ge Rising starts this too: add Mistva, then place it in a Pendulum Zone yourself (step 2).
  • Before step 3, put the Anva from your hand in your other Pendulum Zone. If they chain Ash Blossom to War Zone, Anva negates it.
  • After War Zone you can only Special Summon Dragons, Dinosaurs, Sea Serpents and Wyrms this turn.
Line C — Ringowurm adds a Level 12

Ringowurm is a Level 2 Tuner. Kaiva is the one monster from Line B that the Realms don't need, so Kaiva + Ringowurm becomes Snake-Eyes Vengeance Dragon, a Level 12 Dragon that War Zone's lock allows. Ringowurm then leaves a Tuner Token behind for next turn.

Starting hand: The Melody of Awakening Dragon, Ringowurm, the Dragon Guarding the Hundred Apples, Nibiru, the Primal Being · Normal Summon: Ringowurm, the Dragon Guarding the Hundred Apples

  1. After Line B, Normal Summon Ringowurm (Level 2 Tuner).
  2. Synchro Summon Snake-Eyes Vengeance Dragon (Level 12) using Ringowurm + Kaiva (Level 10).
  3. You Synchro Summoned this turn: banish Ringowurm from your GY to Special Summon a Hundred Apples Token (Level 2, can be used as a Tuner).

End board: Mistva with three Realms + Snake-Eyes Vengeance Dragon + a Tuner Token. Vengeance Dragon adds a fourth Quick Effect: it moves a monster to the Spell & Trap Zone as a Continuous Spell.

  • Next turn the Token + a Level 10 makes Crimson Dragon. Target Vengeance Dragon with its Quick Effect to swap it for Cosmic Blazar Dragon, which negates an activation, a Summon or an attack.
  • Don't use Mistva as Synchro Material while the Realms are out. Without a Ryu-Ge Pendulum or matching Level 10, nobody can use them.
  • Without War Zone this turn, Ringowurm + Murakumo or Futsu (Level 8) makes Chengying, Chaos Angel or Ruddy Rose Dragon instead.

  • Three Realms mean three different Quick Effects on their turn.
  • Melody, Rising, Prayers and Pre-Preparation are all one-card starts.
  • Every monster that matters has 3000 or more ATK.

  • One copy each of War Zone, Kaiva, Emva and Hakva: a bad draw breaks the Ryu-Ge line.
  • Ringowurm is the only Tuner.
  • Many pieces are Level 8 or 10 and do nothing alone in your hand.

Line A — Reichheart into Tri-Heart

A full board from one card. Reichheart finds the Spell Arrival and becomes Light-Heart, which finds the Field Spell. Reichphobia adds Acro, Arrival brings Reichheart back, and the three monsters Link into Tri-Heart. Tri-Heart then revives Acro and adds Astra.

Starting hand: Scareclaw Reichheart · Normal Summon: Scareclaw Reichheart

  1. Normal Summon Reichheart. It adds Scareclaw Arrival from your Deck.
  2. Link Summon Light-Heart to the Extra Monster Zone using Reichheart. It adds Primitive Planet Reichphobia.
  3. Activate Reichphobia: add Scareclaw Acro from your Deck.
  4. Activate Arrival: Special Summon Reichheart from your GY in Defense Position.
  5. Special Summon Acro from your hand to the zone below Light-Heart or next to Reichheart.
  6. Link Summon Tri-Heart to the Extra Monster Zone using Light-Heart + Reichheart + Acro. Every face-up monster becomes Defense Position.
  7. Tri-Heart's effect: Special Summon Acro from your GY and add Scareclaw Astra. You can only Special Summon Scareclaws for the rest of the turn.
  8. Special Summon Astra from your hand next to Acro.

End board: Tri-Heart (3600 ATK) + Acro + Astra + Reichphobia, and you still hold your other 4 cards. Anything they Summon face-up goes to Defense Position, and Tri-Heart ignores those monsters' activated effects. Their monsters lose 100 ATK/DEF per Defense Position monster.

  • Reichphobia (adds Reichheart) and Reinforcement of the Army start the same line.
  • Reichheart's search is once per turn, so the copy Arrival brings back doesn't search again.
  • Make any non-Scareclaw Extra Deck monster before step 7.
Line B — Fenrir first

Kashtira Fenrir Summons itself only while you control no monsters, so it comes before the Scareclaws. It adds Scareclaw Kashtira, a monster you keep in hand and Summon as a Quick Effect on their turn. Then Line A goes ahead as normal. Fenrir doesn't restrict it.

Starting hand: Kashtira Fenrir, Scareclaw Reichheart · Normal Summon: Scareclaw Reichheart

  1. You control no monsters: Special Summon Kashtira Fenrir from your hand.
  2. Fenrir's effect: add Scareclaw Kashtira from your Deck.
  3. Play Line A with Reichheart, ending on Tri-Heart + Acro + Astra. Fenrir moves to Defense Position but keeps its effects.
  4. Their Main Phase: Special Summon Scareclaw Kashtira from your hand (Quick Effect), then banish 1 Scareclaw card from your GY.
  5. When they activate a monster effect, Fenrir banishes 1 face-up card they control, face-down.

End board: Tri-Heart + Fenrir + Acro + Astra, with Scareclaw Kashtira arriving on their turn. Any monster that battles your Scareclaw or Kashtira monsters has its effects negated for the turn.

  • Don't add Kashtira Unicorn in step 2 unless you have Kashtira Birth. It can't Summon itself while Fenrir is on your field.
  • Fenrir counts as a Defense Position monster for Acro's ATK boost and Reichphobia.
  • Two Level 7s can overlay into Kashtira Shangri-Ira, but do it before Tri-Heart's lock.
Line C — Tri-Heart attack (going second)

The same board, used to win the turn you build it. With three different Scareclaws in Defense Position, Tri-Heart attacks three times. Acro gives it 300 ATK for each of your Defense Position monsters, and Belone makes its attacks pierce. Tri-Heart has already turned their monsters to Defense Position, so they have no ATK to hit back with.

Starting hand: Scareclaw Reichheart, Scareclaw Belone · Normal Summon: Scareclaw Reichheart

  1. Play Line A: Tri-Heart in the Extra Monster Zone with Acro and Astra in Defense Position.
  2. Special Summon Belone from your hand next to a Scareclaw. It is a Scareclaw, so Tri-Heart's lock allows it.
  3. 3 or more Defense Position monsters are on the field: Reichphobia destroys 1 card they control.
  4. Attack with Tri-Heart: 3000 + 900 from Acro = 3900 ATK, up to 3 attacks (Acro, Astra and Belone are three names).
  5. Each attack into a Defense Position monster pierces because of Belone. When their monsters run out, it attacks directly.

End board: Three attacks at 3900 ATK. Their monsters are in Defense Position and have lost 100 DEF for every Defense Position monster on the field, so most of each attack goes through as damage.

  • Use Super Polymerization and Infinite Impermanence before you start. A negated Reichheart ends the turn.
  • Astra counts different names: two Acros are still one attack.
  • Reichphobia's destroy is once per turn.
Going second — Super Polymerization

Super Polymerization is a Quick-Play Spell: discard 1 card, then Fusion Summon using monsters from either field. Neither player can respond to it. Two of their best monsters (or one of theirs and one of yours) become one Fusion Monster on your side. The materials are sent to the GY without being targeted or destroyed, so their protection doesn't help. Pick the Fusion by what the two monsters share:

  • Two DARK monsters (no Tokens): Starving Venom Fusion Dragon. Gains the ATK of one of their Special Summoned monsters this turn, and can copy the name and effects of a Level 5+ monster they control. Your own: Reichheart, Light-Heart and Tri-Heart are all DARK.
  • Same Type and same Attribute: Garura, Wings of Resonant Life. Any 2 monsters with different names. Garura doubles the battle damage it deals and draws you 1 card when it goes to the GY. Your own pair: two different Level 3 Scareclaws (EARTH Beasts), or Fenrir + Scareclaw Kashtira (EARTH Psychics).
  • Same Attribute, different Types: Mudragon of the Swamp. Your opponent can't target Mudragon, or any monster sharing its Attribute, with card effects. Your own pair: a Level 3 Scareclaw (Beast) + Fenrir (Psychic), both EARTH.
  • Same Type, different Attributes: Favorite HERO Flame Wingman. Gains 1000 ATK when it battles a monster with 2200+ ATK, and can Fusion Summon again after a monster is destroyed by battle. Your own pair: Fenrir (EARTH) + Unicorn (WIND), both Psychic.
  • You choose the Fusion when Super Polymerization resolves, so check each monster's Type and Attribute before you activate it.
  • Use it before Tri-Heart's revive effect: that lock stops non-Scareclaw Special Summons, Fusions included.
  • You can also Set it and activate it on your opponent's turn, in the middle of their combo.

• Reichheart, Reichphobia and Reinforcement of the Army are all one-card combos into Tri-Heart.

  • Kashtira is a second opening that doesn't use the Normal Summon.
  • 17 hand traps and breakers, including 3 Super Polymerization.

  • Tri-Heart's revive effect locks you to Scareclaws for the turn.
  • Fenrir and Unicorn are weak draws once you already control a monster.
  • Light-Heart's revival from the GY works once per Duel.

earthbound-resonator.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Soul Resonator into Crimson King and Abyss

A one-card combo. Soul Resonator finds Bone Archfiend, and their Levels (3 + 5) make The Crimson King. The King finds Power Vice Dragon, which finds Darkness Resonator, and those two make Scarred. Crimson Gaia adds a Vision Resonator, Darkness lowers it to Level 1, and Scarred + Vision becomes Abyss.

Starting hand: Soul Resonator, Nibiru, the Primal Being · Normal Summon: Soul Resonator

  1. Normal Summon Soul Resonator. It adds Bone Archfiend from your Deck.
  2. Send 1 other card from your hand (here Nibiru) to the GY to Special Summon Bone Archfiend.
  3. Bone Archfiend's effect: send Vision Resonator from your Deck to the GY and make Bone Level 5. Vision adds Crimson Gaia.
  4. Synchro Summon The Crimson King (Level 8) using Soul (3, Tuner) + Bone (5). It adds Power Vice Dragon.
  5. All your monsters are DARK Synchros: Special Summon Power Vice Dragon. It adds Darkness Resonator.
  6. Reveal Red Dragon Archfiend in your Extra Deck to Special Summon Darkness Resonator from your hand.
  7. Activate Crimson Gaia. Its effect adds your second Vision Resonator from the Deck.
  8. A Level 5+ DARK monster is on the field: Special Summon Vision Resonator from your hand.
  9. Darkness Resonator's effect: target Vision Resonator and change its Level to 1.
  10. Synchro Summon Scarred Dragon Archfiend (Level 8) using Darkness (3, Tuner) + Power Vice (5).
  11. Synchro Summon Abyss (Level 9) using Vision (now Level 1, Tuner) + Scarred (8).

End board: The Crimson King + Abyss + Crimson Gaia. Abyss negates 1 face-up card as a Quick Effect. When they activate a monster effect, the King banishes itself to Summon Red Dragon Archfiend at 6000 ATK, safe from destruction by effects. Soul Resonator in your GY can be banished to save a card from being destroyed.

  • Going second: when Scarred is used for Abyss in step 11, use its effect. It Summons Red Dragon Archfiend and destroys all their Attack Position monsters, and you attack with three Dragons.
  • Going first, skip that effect. Red Dragon Archfiend would destroy your other monsters in the End Phase.
  • Every Extra Deck monster here is a DARK Dragon Synchro, so all four locks are satisfied.
Line B — Red Nova Dragon on their turn

Earthbound Immortal Red Nova is a Quick Effect from your hand or GY. It sends a Red Dragon Archfiend you control to the GY and Summons Red Nova Dragon in its place. Scarred counts as Red Dragon Archfiend, and being sent to the GY triggers Scarred, so you get the real Red Dragon Archfiend as well.

Starting hand: Soul Resonator, Earthbound Immortal Red Nova · Normal Summon: Soul Resonator

  1. Play Line A up to step 10 and stop: you control The Crimson King + Scarred. In step 2, send Red Nova as Bone Archfiend's cost.
  2. Their Main Phase, Quick Effect: banish Red Nova from your GY and send Scarred (named Red Dragon Archfiend) from your field to the GY.
  3. Red Nova's effect continues: Special Summon Red Nova Dragon from your Extra Deck. This counts as a Synchro Summon.
  4. Scarred was sent from the field to the GY: Special Summon Red Dragon Archfiend from your Extra Deck.

End board: Red Nova Dragon + Red Dragon Archfiend + The Crimson King on their turn. Red Nova Dragon gains 500 ATK for each Tuner in your GY (3 here, so 5000), can't be destroyed by their card effects, and can banish itself to negate an attack.

  • Red Nova works from your hand in the same way. It is once per turn.
  • Summoning on their turn avoids Red Dragon Archfiend's End Phase effect, which only happens in your End Phase.
  • Red Dragon Archfiend is now out of the Extra Deck, so The Crimson King's Summon effect has nothing to bring out.
Line C — Horus opening

The Horus cards work with no Normal Summon and no Extra Deck, so they are the play when Soul Resonator is missing or gets negated. Imsety's cost sends Vision Resonator, which searches Crimson Gaia. King's Sarcophagus sends Hapi, and both Level 8s Summon themselves from the GY.

Starting hand: Imsety, Glory of Horus, Vision Resonator, Bone Archfiend · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Imsety's effect: send it and Vision Resonator from your hand to the GY. Add King's Sarcophagus, then draw 1.
  2. Vision Resonator was sent to the GY: add Crimson Gaia.
  3. Activate King's Sarcophagus. Send Bone Archfiend from your hand to the GY to send Hapi from your Deck to the GY.
  4. You control King's Sarcophagus: Special Summon Imsety, then Hapi, from your GY.
  5. Activate Crimson Gaia and add Soul Resonator. Your Normal Summon is still free for Line A.

End board: Imsety + Hapi + King's Sarcophagus + Crimson Gaia, with Soul Resonator in hand and Bone Archfiend in the GY. Horus monsters can't be destroyed by effects that don't target them, and they return from the GY every turn.

  • If you continue into Line A, Bone Archfiend Summons itself from the GY by sending 1 card.
  • King's Sarcophagus can send up to 4 times a turn. Each card sent as a cost can be a Resonator piece you want in the GY.
  • Imsety and Hapi each Summon themselves from the GY once per turn.
Going second — Super Polymerization

Super Polymerization is a Quick-Play Spell: discard 1 card, then Fusion Summon using monsters from either field. Neither player can respond to it. Two of their best monsters (or one of theirs and one of yours) become one Fusion Monster on your side. The materials are sent to the GY without being targeted or destroyed, so their protection doesn't help. Pick the Fusion by what the two monsters share:

  • Same Type and same Attribute: Garura, Wings of Resonant Life. Any 2 monsters with different names. Garura doubles the battle damage it deals and draws you 1 card when it goes to the GY. Your own pair: Bone Archfiend + Stone Sweeper (DARK Fiends).
  • Same Attribute, different Types: Mudragon of the Swamp. Your opponent can't target Mudragon, or any monster sharing its Attribute, with card effects. Your own pair: Imsety (Spellcaster) + Bone Archfiend (Fiend), both DARK.
  • Same Type, different Attributes: Favorite HERO Flame Wingman. Gains 1000 ATK when it battles a monster with 2200+ ATK, and can Fusion Summon again after a monster is destroyed by battle. Your own pair: Soul Resonator (FIRE) + Bone Archfiend (DARK), both Fiends.
  • Use it before any Resonator effect, or on their turn. The Resonator locks stop Fusion Summons for the rest of that turn.
  • You choose the Fusion when Super Polymerization resolves, so check each monster's Type and Attribute first.
  • Imsety is the best discard: it can Summon itself from the GY once King's Sarcophagus is out.
earthbound-resonator.str:
• Ten cards lead to Soul Resonator, and it is a one-card combo.

  • Red Nova Dragon arrives at Quick Effect speed on either turn.
  • The Horus engine is a complete second plan that ignores the Resonator locks.

  • One copy each of Red Dragon Archfiend, Darkness Resonator and Power Vice Dragon.
  • Red Dragon Archfiend destroys your own monsters in the End Phase if they didn't attack.
  • Horus cards and Level 12s can clog a hand that has no starter.

primite-blue-eyes.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Sage into Blue-Eyes Spirit Dragon

One Normal Summon. Sage finds Maiden and becomes the Link Monster Spirit, which finds the Field Spell Mausoleum. Mausoleum lets you Normal Summon Maiden as well and sends a Blue-Eyes to the GY. Maiden places True Light. Spirit Tributes itself to revive Blue-Eyes, Maiden returns, and the two make Spirit Dragon.

Starting hand: Sage with Eyes of Blue · Normal Summon: Sage with Eyes of Blue

  1. Normal Summon Sage. It adds Maiden of White from your Deck.
  2. Link Summon Spirit with Eyes of Blue using Sage. It adds Mausoleum of White. Activate Mausoleum.
  3. Mausoleum gives an extra Normal Summon for a Level 1 LIGHT Tuner: Normal Summon Maiden.
  4. Mausoleum's effect: target Spirit and send Blue-Eyes White Dragon from your Deck to the GY.
  5. Maiden's effect: send her from the field to the GY and place True Light face-up from your Deck.
  6. Tribute Spirit with Eyes of Blue: Special Summon Blue-Eyes from your GY. Maiden then Special Summons herself from the GY.
  7. Synchro Summon Blue-Eyes Spirit Dragon (Level 9) using Maiden (1, Tuner) + Blue-Eyes (8).
  8. True Light's effect: Special Summon Blue-Eyes from your GY.

End board: Spirit Dragon + Blue-Eyes White Dragon + True Light. Spirit Dragon negates one GY effect each turn. Then, on their turn, Tribute it to Summon Ultimate Spirit Dragon, which negates one card or effect activated on the field. They can't target Blue-Eyes White Dragon while True Light is face-up.

  • Tribute Spirit with Eyes of Blue before Maiden needs to return. While Spirit is on the field you can only Special Summon Dragons.
  • The monster Spirit Dragon Summons is destroyed in the End Phase. When Ultimate Spirit Dragon is destroyed, it revives a LIGHT Dragon from your GY.
  • Wishes for Eyes of Blue starts this line too: it adds Sage plus True Light or Roar.
Line B — Primite opening

The second engine, using only the Normal Summon. Ether Beryl Sets Lordly Lode from the Deck. Lode searches Drillbeam and then Summons Blue-Eyes White Dragon straight from the Deck. With a Normal Monster on the field, Drillbeam needs nothing revealed: it negates and banishes a card on their turn.

Starting hand: Primite Dragon Ether Beryl · Normal Summon: Primite Dragon Ether Beryl

  1. Normal Summon Ether Beryl. It Sets Primite Lordly Lode from your Deck.
  2. Activate Lordly Lode: add Primite Drillbeam from your Deck.
  3. Lode's effect: name Blue-Eyes White Dragon and Special Summon it from your Deck in Defense Position.
  4. Tribute Ether Beryl: send a second Blue-Eyes from your Deck to the GY. (Beryl was Normal Summoned, so Lode's restriction doesn't stop it.)
  5. Set Primite Drillbeam.

End board: Blue-Eyes White Dragon (3300 ATK with Lode) + Lordly Lode + a Set Drillbeam, with a second Blue-Eyes in the GY. On their turn Drillbeam negates and banishes 1 face-up card. In your Standby Phase, Ether Beryl returns to your hand.

  • After Lode's Summon effect, Special Summoned monsters on the field can't activate effects this turn. Finish Line A first if you have both.
  • Drillbeam can Set itself from the GY in your Main Phase while you control a Primite monster.
  • The Blue-Eyes in the GY is ready for True Light, Spirit with Eyes of Blue or Indigo-Eyes next turn.
Line C — Tyrant Dragon (going second)

A Fusion boss with no Fusion Spell. Wishes finds Sage and Roar, and Roar Summons Blue-Eyes from the Deck. Wishes then works a second time from the GY: it equips a Fusion Monster to Blue-Eyes. A Blue-Eyes equipped with a Fusion can be Tributed for Tyrant Dragon, which attacks every monster they control.

Starting hand: Wishes for Eyes of Blue, Droll & Lock Bird · Normal Summon: Sage with Eyes of Blue

  1. Activate Wishes: discard 1 card (here Droll) and add Sage and Roar of the Blue-Eyed Dragons.
  2. Activate Roar: Special Summon Blue-Eyes White Dragon from your Deck in Defense Position.
  3. Banish Wishes from your GY: equip Neo Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon from your Extra Deck to Blue-Eyes.
  4. Tribute that Blue-Eyes to Special Summon Blue-Eyes Tyrant Dragon from your Extra Deck.
  5. Normal Summon Sage and add Maiden of White for next turn.
  6. Tyrant Dragon (3400 ATK) attacks each of their monsters once. After it battles, it Sets a Trap from your GY.

End board: Tyrant Dragon has attacked every monster they control and is unaffected by their Traps. You keep Maiden in hand and Sage on the field.

  • Roar only lets you Special Summon Dragons from the Extra Deck this turn. Tyrant is a Dragon.
  • Wishes' search and its GY effect are separate effects, so both work in the same turn.
  • If a Blue-Eyes is already in your GY, Roar can bring that one back instead.
Line D — Indigo-Eyes for 8000 (going second)

Two Blue-Eyes White Dragons overlay into Indigo-Eyes Silver Dragon. When it is Xyz Summoned it negates every face-up card your opponent controls. It then detaches a Blue-Eyes and revives it with 1000 extra ATK. Two 4000 ATK Dragons deal exactly 8000.

Starting hand: Wishes for Eyes of Blue, Droll & Lock Bird · Normal Summon: Sage with Eyes of Blue

  1. Activate Wishes: discard 1 card and add Sage and Roar. Activate Roar: Special Summon Blue-Eyes from your Deck.
  2. Normal Summon Sage (add Maiden), then Link Summon Spirit with Eyes of Blue using Sage and add Mausoleum.
  3. Activate Mausoleum. Its effect sends a second Blue-Eyes from your Deck to the GY.
  4. Tribute Spirit with Eyes of Blue: Special Summon that Blue-Eyes from your GY.
  5. Xyz Summon Indigo-Eyes Silver Dragon using both Blue-Eyes. Its effect negates all face-up cards they control.
  6. Detach 1 Blue-Eyes, then Special Summon it from the GY with 1000 extra ATK (4000).
  7. Attack with Indigo-Eyes (4000) and Blue-Eyes (4000).

End board: Their whole field is negated for the turn and you attack for 8000. Indigo-Eyes still has one Blue-Eyes attached, which it needs in order to attack directly.

  • Don't use Lordly Lode's Summon effect this turn. It would stop Indigo-Eyes from activating its negate.
  • Each Indigo-Eyes effect is once per turn.
  • If they still have monsters, use Lightning Storm or Majesty of the White Dragons first so the attacks are direct.
primite-blue-eyes.str:
• Two separate starting engines: the Eyes of Blue Tuners and Primite.
  • Spirit Dragon into Ultimate Spirit Dragon gives two negates from one monster.
  • Indigo-Eyes negates an entire field and sets up exactly 8000 damage.
  • Lightning Storm ×2, Majesty and Primite Drillbeam ×2 for going second.

  • Removing True Light destroys your own board.
  • Three Blue-Eyes White Dragons in the Deck are bad draws without a way to discard or Summon them.
  • Several of your own cards restrict what you can Summon or activate that turn.

swordsoul-tenyi.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Mo Ye + Longyuan into Chixiao and Chengying

The standard two-card play. Mo Ye reveals Longyuan to get a Token, and the two make Chixiao (4 + 4 = 8). Chixiao searches Taia, which becomes Longyuan's discard. Longyuan brings its own Token and they make a Level 10 (4 + 6). You draw a card and deal 1200 damage along the way.

Starting hand: Swordsoul of Mo Ye, Swordsoul Strategist Longyuan · Normal Summon: Swordsoul of Mo Ye

  1. Normal Summon Mo Ye. Reveal Longyuan in your hand to Special Summon a Swordsoul Token (Level 4 Tuner).
  2. Synchro Summon Chixiao (Level 8) using the Token + Mo Ye. Mo Ye, as material, draws you 1 card.
  3. Chixiao was Synchro Summoned: add Swordsoul of Taia from your Deck.
  4. Longyuan's effect: discard Taia to Special Summon Longyuan and a second Token.
  5. Synchro Summon Chengying (Level 10) using the Token + Longyuan. Longyuan, as material, deals 1200 damage.

End board: Chixiao + Chengying. On their turn Chixiao banishes Mo Ye or Taia from your GY to negate a monster's effects, and that banish triggers Chengying: banish 1 card from their field and 1 from their GY. If an effect would destroy Chengying, banish a card from your GY instead.

  • Chixiao gets one effect per turn. It searched on your turn, so its negate is ready on their turn.
  • Against Spell/Trap-heavy decks make Qixing Longyuan as your Level 10 instead: it banishes a Spell/Trap they activate and a monster they Special Summon.
  • If Chixiao's search is negated, Longyuan can discard any other Swordsoul card or Wyrm.
Line B — Tenyi start into Psychic End Punisher

Tenyi Spirits Summon themselves while you control no Effect Monsters, so Vishuda comes first. Mo Ye's Token + Vishuda (4 + 7) makes Psychic End Punisher. Suruya + Mo Ye makes Chixiao, and Suruya then Summons Monk of the Tenyi at a cost of 1000 LP. That cost is useful: Psychic End Punisher is protected while your LP are lower.

Starting hand: Tenyi Spirit - Vishuda, Tenyi Spirit - Suruya, Swordsoul of Mo Ye · Normal Summon: Swordsoul of Mo Ye

  1. You control no Effect Monsters: Special Summon Vishuda from your hand.
  2. Normal Summon Mo Ye. Reveal Suruya (a Wyrm) to Special Summon a Swordsoul Token.
  3. You control a Wyrm: Special Summon Suruya (Level 4 Tuner) from your hand.
  4. Synchro Summon Psychic End Punisher (Level 11) using the Token + Vishuda (7).
  5. Synchro Summon Chixiao (Level 8) using Suruya (Tuner) + Mo Ye. Mo Ye draws 1 and Chixiao adds a Swordsoul card.
  6. Suruya was material for a Wyrm Synchro: Special Summon Monk of the Tenyi from your Extra Deck. You lose 1000 LP.

End board: Psychic End Punisher (3500 ATK) + Chixiao + Monk. Your LP are lower than theirs, so Psychic End Punisher is unaffected by their activated effects. Chixiao negates a monster on their turn. Monk has no effect, so next turn you can banish Vishuda from your GY to return 1 of their cards to the hand.

  • Use the Token in step 4 before Monk arrives. While a Token is on the field only Synchros can come from the Extra Deck, and Monk is a Link.
  • Psychic End Punisher's protection only applies while your LP are equal to or lower than theirs.
  • Each Tenyi's Summon and its banish effect are once per turn.
Line C — Ecclesia going second

When they control more monsters than you, Incredible Ecclesia Summons herself from your hand. She Tributes herself to bring Mo Ye from the Deck, so your Normal Summon is still free. Chixiao negates their best monster, then Taia and a second Token make Baxia, which shuffles two of their cards into the Deck.

Starting hand: Harpie's Feather Duster, Incredible Ecclesia, the Virtuous, Swordsoul Emergence · Normal Summon: Swordsoul of Taia

  1. Activate Harpie's Feather Duster: destroy all their Spells and Traps.
  2. They control more monsters: Special Summon Incredible Ecclesia from your hand.
  3. Ecclesia's Quick Effect: Tribute her to Special Summon Mo Ye from your Deck. Mo Ye reveals Emergence for a Token.
  4. Synchro Summon Chixiao using the Token + Mo Ye. Mo Ye draws 1. Don't use Chixiao's search.
  5. Chixiao's Quick Effect: banish Mo Ye from your GY to negate 1 of their Effect Monsters.
  6. Activate Emergence: add Taia and Normal Summon it. Taia banishes Emergence from your GY for a Token.
  7. Synchro Summon Baxia (Level 8) using the Token (WATER) + Taia (WIND): two Attributes, so shuffle 2 of their cards into the Deck.

End board: Chixiao (2800) + Baxia (2300) facing a field with no Spells or Traps, its best monster negated and two more cards shuffled away. Attack with both.

  • Skip Chixiao's search here: it can only use one effect per turn and you need the negate now.
  • Baxia counts the Attributes of the Wyrms used. Token (WATER) + Taia (WIND) is two. Token + Mo Ye (both WATER) is one.
  • Shuffling into the Deck doesn't destroy or send to the GY, so most protection doesn't stop it.
swordsoul-tenyi.str:
• Nine Swordsoul monsters plus three Emergence, so the deck almost always has a Token.
  • Chixiao and Chengying together negate and banish from a single activation.
  • Evenly Matched, Feather Duster, Nibiru and 8 other hand traps for going second.
  • Bonuses on Synchro Material (draw, send, 1200 damage) keep the hand full.

  • Mo Ye and Longyuan each need another Swordsoul card or Wyrm in hand.
  • Your own Effect Monsters switch off the Tenyi self-Summons.
  • Only 5 Spells, so few ways to recover from a negated Normal Summon.

Line A — Swordsoul into Qixing Longyuan (going first)

The going-first board. Mo Ye and Longyuan each bring a Token. Longyuan + Token makes Qixing Longyuan first, so that when Mo Ye + Token then makes Chixiao, Qixing draws you a card for Synchro Summoning another Wyrm. You end with two draws and 1200 damage dealt.

Starting hand: Swordsoul of Mo Ye, Swordsoul Strategist Longyuan, Swordsoul of Taia · Normal Summon: Swordsoul of Mo Ye

  1. Normal Summon Mo Ye. Reveal Longyuan to Special Summon a Swordsoul Token (Level 4 Tuner).

End board: Qixing Longyuan + Chixiao + a Set Blackout. When they Special Summon, Qixing banishes that monster for 1200 damage. When they activate a Spell or Trap, it banishes that card for another 1200. Chixiao negates a monster by banishing Taia or Mo Ye from your GY.

  • Chixiao gets one effect per turn: it searched on your turn, so the negate is ready on theirs.
  • While a Token is on the field you can only Special Summon Synchros from the Extra Deck.
  • Blackout destroys one of your own Wyrms along with 2 of their cards. Use it when a Synchro is about to be removed anyway.
Line B — Tenpai Battle Phase win (going second)

The Tenpai Dragons do their work during the Battle Phase. Paidra finds the Field Spell, which finds Chundra. When Paidra attacks, Chundra brings Fadra from the Deck. Chundra + Paidra then Synchro into Bident Dragion, and Bident + Fadra into Transcendent Dragion. From that point they can't activate anything.

Starting hand: Tenpai Dragon Paidra, Effect Veiler · Normal Summon: Tenpai Dragon Paidra

  1. Normal Summon Paidra. It adds Sangen Summoning from your Deck.
  2. Activate Sangen Summoning. Its effect adds Chundra, then you discard 1 card (here Effect Veiler).
  3. You control a FIRE Dragon: Special Summon Chundra from your hand.
  4. Battle Phase: Paidra attacks. At the start of the Damage Step, Chundra Special Summons Fadra from your Deck.
  5. Chundra's Quick Effect: Synchro Summon Bident Dragion (Level 7) using Chundra (4, Tuner) + Paidra (3).
  6. Bident was Synchro Summoned: Special Summon Paidra from your GY. Only Dragons can be Special Summoned from now on.
  7. Fadra's Quick Effect: Synchro Summon Transcendent Dragion (Level 10) using Bident (7, Tuner) + Fadra (3).
  8. Transcendent changes all monsters to Attack Position. Attack with Transcendent (3000) and Paidra (1700). They can't respond.
  9. 3 attacks have been declared: Special Summon Bident from your GY, destroy 1 Spell/Trap, and attack with it (2600).

End board: Four attacks in one Battle Phase for 1700 + 3000 + 1700 + 2600 = 9000 damage if they are direct. Their monsters are forced into Attack Position, and nothing can be activated against you once Transcendent Dragion is out.

  • Clear their monsters first with Lightning Storm or Widow Anchor so the attacks are direct.
  • Paidra means you take no battle damage from your FIRE Dragons' battles, so attacking into a bigger monster to start the chain is safe.
  • Bident's return from the GY is once per Duel.
Line C — Sky Striker first (going second)

Sky Striker Spells need your Main Monster Zones empty, so they are the first thing you play. Hornet Drones makes a Token, the Token becomes Kagari in the Extra Monster Zone, and Kagari returns Engage to your hand. With 3 Spells in the GY, Widow Anchor takes their best monster, and you Link it away.

Starting hand: Lightning Storm, Sky Striker Mobilize - Engage!, Sky Striker Mecha - Widow Anchor · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. You control no face-up cards: activate Lightning Storm and destroy all their Spells and Traps.
  2. Activate Engage!: add Hornet Drones from your Deck.
  3. Activate Hornet Drones: Special Summon a Sky Striker Ace Token.
  4. Link Summon Kagari to the Extra Monster Zone using the Token. Kagari returns Engage! from your GY to your hand.
  5. Your Main Monster Zones are empty again: activate Engage! and add your second Widow Anchor.
  6. Activate Widow Anchor with 3 Spells in your GY: negate their best Effect Monster and take control of it.
  7. Link Summon Camellia using the stolen monster + Kagari. Their monster is gone for good.

End board: Camellia in the Extra Monster Zone, their backrow destroyed and their best monster used as Link Material. You still hold a Widow Anchor and your Normal Summon: Summon Paidra and go to Line B.

  • Count the Spells in your GY. Widow Anchor only takes control with 3 or more there when it resolves.
  • Kagari and Camellia can each be Special Summoned once per turn.
  • Lightning Storm needs you to control no face-up cards, so it comes before everything else.
tenpai-wyrm.str:
• Three engines, so one hand trap rarely stops the whole turn.
  • Paidra is a one-card start to a Battle Phase the opponent can't respond in.
  • Qixing Longyuan and Chixiao give a real going-first board.
  • Widow Anchor and Lightning Storm work from an empty field.

  • Sky Striker Spells are dead once you have Main Monster Zone monsters.
  • The Tenpai half does nothing going first, when there is no Battle Phase.

  1. Activate Synchro Fellowship: add Junk Synchron and Full-Speed Warrior, then discard Full-Speed Warrior.
  2. Normal Summon Junk Synchron. It Special Summons Full-Speed Warrior from your GY.
  3. Synchro Summon Junk Speeder (Level 5) to the Extra Monster Zone using Junk Synchron (3) + Full-Speed Warrior (2).
  4. Junk Speeder's effect: Special Summon 5 Tuners from your Deck: Scrap (Level 1), Assault (2), Junk (3), Stardust (4) and Wheel Synchron (5).
  5. Stardust Synchron was Summoned: add your second Synchro Fellowship for next turn.
  6. Synchro Summon Clear Wing (Level 7) using Assault (2, Tuner) + Junk Speeder (5).
  7. Synchro Summon Accel Synchro Stardust Dragon (Level 8) using Junk Synchron (3) + Wheel (5, as a non-Tuner). It revives Assault.
  8. Their Main Phase: Tribute Accel to Special Summon Stardust Dragon from your Extra Deck, then Synchro Summon immediately.
  9. That Synchro Summon: Satellite Warrior (Level 10) using Assault (2) + Stardust Dragon (8). Destroy up to 3 of their cards.

End board: End your turn on Clear Wing + Accel with Assault, Scrap and Stardust Synchron beside them. Clear Wing negates a Level 5+ monster's effect. Accel then becomes Satellite Warrior in the middle of their turn: 3 Synchros are in your GY, so it destroys 3 cards, reaches 5500 ATK and is unaffected by their effects that turn.

  • Count Levels before each Synchro. The only non-Tuners are Junk Speeder and Wheel Synchron, so each can pay for one Synchro.
  • If you would rather keep Stardust Dragon's negate, skip Accel's revive in step 7. With Assault in the GY, banish it when Accel is Tributed and Accel comes back.
  • You can only activate 1 Synchro Fellowship per turn.
Line B — Junk Converter + any Tuner

The two-card version, and the reason hand traps are never dead here. Junk Converter discards itself with any Tuner to find Junk Synchron. Junk Synchron revives Converter, and they make Junk Speeder. Converter, used as material, then brings the discarded Tuner back too.

Starting hand: Junk Converter, Effect Veiler · Normal Summon: Junk Synchron

  1. Junk Converter's effect: discard it and Effect Veiler (a Tuner) to add Junk Synchron.
  2. Normal Summon Junk Synchron. It Special Summons Junk Converter (Level 2) from your GY.
  3. Synchro Summon Junk Speeder to the Extra Monster Zone using Junk Synchron + Junk Converter.
  4. Junk Converter was used as Synchro Material: Special Summon Effect Veiler from your GY in Defense Position.
  5. Junk Speeder's effect: Special Summon Assault, Junk, Stardust and Wheel Synchron from your Deck (4 zones are free).
  6. Continue from Line A step 5: Clear Wing, then Accel Synchro Stardust Dragon.

End board: The Line A board with Effect Veiler (a Level 1 Tuner) in Scrap Synchron's place: Clear Wing + Accel + three Tuners.

  • Any Tuner pays for Junk Converter: Ash Blossom, Effect Veiler, Ghost Ogre or a Synchron you don't need.
  • The Tuner that Converter revives can't activate its effects this turn, but it is a body for a Synchro.
  • Each Junk Converter effect is once per turn.
Line C — Satellite Warrior (going second)

The board breaker. Satellite Warrior destroys one card for every Synchro Monster in your GY, so you make two cheap Synchros first and use one as its material. Stardust Charge Warrior draws a card on the way, and Accel stays on the field as a second attacker.

Starting hand: Synchro Fellowship · Normal Summon: Junk Synchron

  1. Play Line A steps 1–5: Junk Speeder + five Tuners (Scrap, Assault, Junk, Stardust, Wheel).
  2. Synchro Summon Stardust Charge Warrior (Level 6) using Scrap (1) + Junk Speeder (5). Draw 1.
  3. Synchro Summon Accel Synchro Stardust Dragon (Level 8) using Junk Synchron (3) + Wheel (5, as a non-Tuner). It revives Scrap.
  4. Synchro Summon Satellite Warrior (Level 10) using Stardust Synchron (4) + Charge Warrior (6).
  5. Satellite Warrior's effect: Junk Speeder and Charge Warrior are in your GY, so destroy 2 of their cards. It gains 2000 ATK.
  6. Attack with Satellite Warrior (4500) and Accel (2500).

End board: Two of their cards destroyed, then 7000 damage from Satellite Warrior and Accel. If Satellite Warrior is destroyed later, it revives up to 3 Warrior, Synchron or Stardust Synchros from your GY.

  • Synchro Emergency can set this up on their turn: Summon a monster from your hand and Junk Synchron from the Deck, then banish Emergency from the GY to Synchro Summon Junk Speeder.
  • More Synchros in the GY means more destroys. A third cheap Synchro before Satellite Warrior makes it 3.
  • Assault and Scrap are still on the field as Tuners for your next turn.

Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Zoa + Metal Claws into Metalzoa X

Two cards and no Normal Summon. Zoa Summons itself and Sets Max Metalmorph from the Deck. Metal Claws Summons itself by sending that face-down Trap to the GY, then adds a second copy. With Metal Claws on the field you can activate the new copy the same turn: Tribute Zoa, a Level 7 Fiend, for Metalzoa X.

Starting hand: Zoa the Fiendish Beast, Red-Eyes Metal Claws Dragon · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Special Summon Zoa from your hand in Defense Position. (Your opponent may Special Summon 1 monster from their hand.)
  2. Zoa's effect: Set Max Metalmorph from your Deck.
  3. Send that face-down Max Metalmorph to the GY to Special Summon Metal Claws from your hand.
  4. Metal Claws was Summoned with Max in your GY: add a second Max Metalmorph from your Deck, and Set it.
  5. Activate Max Metalmorph (Metal Claws allows it this turn): Tribute Zoa to Special Summon Metalzoa X from your Deck.
  6. Max Metalmorph equips to Metalzoa X: +400 ATK, safe from destruction and targeting by monster effects and Spells.

End board: Metalzoa X (3400 ATK, protected) + Metal Claws, with your Normal Summon unused. Twice per turn, when they activate a monster effect or a Spell, Metalzoa X destroys 1 of their face-up monsters. Metal Claws is ready to be Tributed for Fullmetal next turn.

  • Prefer the negate? Tribute Metal Claws in step 5 instead: a Level 7 Dragon gives Red-Eyes Black Fullmetal Dragon.
  • A Max Metalmorph is now in your GY, so later Zoas no longer give the opponent a free Summon.
  • Incoming Machine! and Metalflame Swordsman both find Zoa or Metal Claws.
Line B — Metal Illusionist into Fullmetal Dragon

The same idea using your Normal Summon. Metal Illusionist Sets Max Metalmorph. Metal Claws sends it to the GY to Summon itself and takes it straight back. You Set it again, activate it at once and Tribute Metal Claws, a Level 7 Dragon, for Red-Eyes Black Fullmetal Dragon.

Starting hand: Metal Illusionist, Red-Eyes Metal Claws Dragon · Normal Summon: Metal Illusionist

  1. Normal Summon Metal Illusionist. It Sets Max Metalmorph from your Deck.
  2. Send the face-down Max Metalmorph to the GY to Special Summon Metal Claws from your hand.
  3. Metal Claws' effect: add Max Metalmorph back from your GY. Set it.
  4. Activate Max Metalmorph: Tribute Metal Claws to Special Summon Red-Eyes Black Fullmetal Dragon from your Deck.
  5. Max Metalmorph equips to Fullmetal Dragon (3800 ATK).

End board: Red-Eyes Black Fullmetal Dragon (3800 ATK, protected) + Metal Illusionist. Once per turn, when they activate a card or effect, Fullmetal negates it, then deals damage equal to the original ATK of one of their Attack Position monsters.

  • Activate Max while Metal Claws is still on the field. Tributing it is the cost, paid after the activation is declared.
  • One for One Summons Metal Illusionist from the Deck if you would rather keep the Normal Summon.
  • On their turn Metal Illusionist is Level 5 and can become a Warrior: a second Max Metalmorph can turn it into Metalflame Swordsman.
Line C — Fiendsmith into Desirae

One Engraver and no Normal Summon. Engraver finds Tract, Tract finds Lurrie, and discarding Lurrie Summons it. Lurrie becomes Requiem, which brings Lacrima from the Deck. A second Engraver returns from the GY, and Engraver + Lacrima make Sequence. Sequence fuses Desirae from the GY, then both Links equip to it.

Starting hand: Fiendsmith Engraver · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Discard Engraver: add Fiendsmith's Tract from your Deck.
  2. Activate Tract: add Fabled Lurrie, then discard it. Lurrie Special Summons itself.
  3. Link Summon Fiendsmith's Requiem using Lurrie.
  4. Tribute Requiem: Special Summon Lacrima from your Deck. Lacrima sends a second Engraver from your Deck to the GY.
  5. Engraver's GY effect: shuffle Lurrie from your GY into the Deck to Special Summon Engraver.
  6. Link Summon Fiendsmith's Sequence using Engraver + Lacrima.
  7. Sequence's effect: shuffle both Engravers and Lacrima from your GY into the Deck to Fusion Summon Desirae.
  8. Equip Sequence (from the field) and Requiem (from the GY) to Desirae.

End board: Fiendsmith's Desirae at 3400 ATK with Link Rating 3 equipped. As a Quick Effect it negates up to 3 face-up cards for the turn, and they can't target it. If it is sent to the GY, it sends 1 card on the field to the GY. It is also a Level 9 Fiend: a later Max Metalmorph turns it into Metalzoa X.

  • Requiem can be Special Summoned only once per turn.
  • Each Engraver effect is once per turn by name: the discard and the GY revival are different effects, so both happen.
  • This line uses no Normal Summon and no Max Metalmorph, so it combines with Line A or B in the same turn.
Going second — Super Polymerization

Super Polymerization is a Quick-Play Spell: discard 1 card, then Fusion Summon using monsters from either field. Neither player can respond to it. Two of their best monsters (or one of theirs and one of yours) become one Fusion Monster on your side. The materials are sent to the GY without being targeted or destroyed, so their protection doesn't help. Pick the Fusion by what the two monsters share:

  • Two DARK monsters (no Tokens): Starving Venom Fusion Dragon. Gains the ATK of one of their Special Summoned monsters this turn, and can copy the name and effects of a Level 5+ monster they control. Your own: Zoa, Metal Claws, Fullmetal and Metalzoa X are all DARK.
  • Same Type and same Attribute: Garura, Wings of Resonant Life. Any 2 monsters with different names. Garura doubles the battle damage it deals and draws you 1 card when it goes to the GY. Your own pair: Metal Claws + Black Metal Dragon (DARK Dragons).
  • Same Attribute, different Types: Mudragon of the Swamp. Your opponent can't target Mudragon, or any monster sharing its Attribute, with card effects. Your own pair: Zoa (Fiend) + Metal Claws (Dragon), both DARK.
  • Same Type, different Attributes: Favorite HERO Flame Wingman. Gains 1000 ATK when it battles a monster with 2200+ ATK, and can Fusion Summon again after a monster is destroyed by battle. Your own pair: Engraver (LIGHT) + Zoa (DARK), both Fiends.
  • You choose the Fusion when Super Polymerization resolves, so check each monster's Type and Attribute first.
  • A Metalmorph boss you can't Summon yet is a fine discard: Max Metalmorph can Summon it from the GY later.
  • You can also Set it and activate it on your opponent's turn, in the middle of their combo.
metalmorph-fiendsmith.str:
• Three bosses for three situations, all fetched by the same Trap.
  • Max Metalmorph's equip protects against monster effects and Spells.
  • Fiendsmith is an independent line that uses no Normal Summon.
  • Fourteen interaction cards, including Droplet and Super Polymerization.
metalmorph-fiendsmith.weak:
• The key card is a Trap: slow without Metal Claws, and exposed while Set.
  • Zoa's own Summon gives the opponent a free monster early on.
  • One copy each of Fullmetal and Metalzoa X, so a banished boss is hard to replace.
  • Many high-Level monsters that do nothing without Max Metalmorph.
