blackwing-angelechy.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Simoon into Full Armor Master and Assault Dragon

Three Blackwings become both bosses. Simoon places Black Whirlwind and finds Vata, and Vata Summons Black-Winged Dragon from the Extra Deck. Sudri comes back from banishment and makes a Tuner Token for Boreastorm. Boreastorm + Black-Winged Dragon is Full Armor Master. Then you banish those two from the GY for Assault Dragon.

Starting hand: Blackwing - Simoon the Poison Wind, Blackwing - Sudri the Phantom Glimmer, Blackwing - Shamal the Sandstorm · Normal Summon: Blackwing - Simoon the Poison Wind

  1. Send Shamal from your hand to the GY to place Black Feather Whirlwind from your Deck.
  2. Simoon's effect: banish Sudri from your hand, place Black Whirlwind from your Deck and Normal Summon Simoon.
  3. Black Whirlwind adds Vata. You control a Blackwing, so Special Summon Vata from your hand.
  4. Vata's effect: send Vata + Sudri + Harmattan from your Deck (Levels 2 + 4 + 2) to Special Summon Black-Winged Dragon.
  5. Black Feather Whirlwind revives the banished Sudri. Shamal banishes itself from the GY to return Vata to your hand.
  6. Sudri's effect: Tribute Simoon to Special Summon a Phantom Glimmer Token (Level 2 Tuner).
  7. Synchro Summon Boreastorm (Level 6) using the Token + Sudri. It sends a Vata from your Deck to the GY and becomes Level 2.
  8. Synchro Summon Full Armor Master (Level 10) using Boreastorm (2, Tuner) + Black-Winged Dragon (8).
  9. Banish Boreastorm and Black-Winged Dragon from your GY to Special Summon Black-Winged Assault Dragon from your Extra Deck.

End board: Full Armor Master (3000) + Assault Dragon (3200) + Black Feather Whirlwind, with Vata in hand. Each monster effect they activate deals 700 damage and marks that monster with a Wedge Counter. On your turn Full Armor Master takes control of one, and with 4 counters Assault Dragon can destroy the whole field on their turn.

  • Shamal's and Sudri's 700 damage becomes counters on Black-Winged Dragon while it is on the field, so you lose no LP for them.
  • In the End Phase the Black Whirlwind placed by Simoon goes to the GY and you take 1000 damage.
  • Everything from the Extra Deck here is a DARK Synchro, which satisfies both Simoon's and Sudri's locks.
Line B — Angelechy in the Spell & Trap Zone

The Angelechy plan with no Normal Summon. Problem Summons Enlisted and places Destrier as a Continuous Spell, and Destrier finds Opposition. Opposition gives the opponent a second Enlisted and places Bastion, which places Shatranga. Your Enlisted then banishes the one you gave away.

Starting hand: Angelechy Problem, Infinite Impermanence · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate Angelechy Problem in your Field Zone.
  2. Problem's effect: discard a Spell/Trap to Special Summon Enlisted and place Destrier as a Continuous Spell.
  3. Destrier was placed as a Continuous Spell: add Angelechy Opposition.
  4. Activate Opposition: Special Summon your second Enlisted to their field, in a column next to yours, and place Bastion.
  5. Bastion was placed: place Shatranga from your Extra Deck as a Continuous Spell.
  6. Your Enlisted's effect: banish their Enlisted. Yours moves to their field, returns to your Extra Deck, and you Special Summon it again.

End board: Enlisted on your field with Destrier, Bastion and Shatranga as Continuous Spells. Each card or effect they activate costs them 500 LP. They can activate only 5 monster effects a turn, and their effects can't destroy your other Angelechy cards.

  • After Opposition you can only Special Summon LIGHT or DARK Synchros from the Extra Deck this turn. The Blackwing line still works.
  • Do this before Simoon or Vata. Their lock allows DARK monsters only, and every Angelechy is LIGHT.
  • Next turn, Angelechy Strategy Score in the GY can Summon Shatranga or Bastion from your Spell & Trap Zone as a 3000 ATK monster.
Going second — Super Polymerization

Super Polymerization is a Quick-Play Spell: discard 1 card, then Fusion Summon using monsters from either field. Neither player can respond to it. Two of their best monsters (or one of theirs and one of yours) become one Fusion Monster on your side. The materials are sent to the GY without being targeted or destroyed, so their protection doesn't help. Pick the Fusion by what the two monsters share:

  • Two DARK monsters (no Tokens): Starving Venom Fusion Dragon. Gains the ATK of one of their Special Summoned monsters this turn, and can copy the name and effects of a Level 5+ monster they control. Your own: every Blackwing and every Blackwing Synchro is DARK.
  • Same Type and same Attribute: Garura, Wings of Resonant Life. Any 2 monsters with different names. Garura doubles the battle damage it deals and draws you 1 card when it goes to the GY. Your own pair: any 2 different Blackwings (DARK Winged Beasts).
  • Same Attribute, different Types: Mudragon of the Swamp. Your opponent can't target Mudragon, or any monster sharing its Attribute, with card effects. Your own pair: a Blackwing (Winged Beast) + Black-Winged Dragon (Dragon), both DARK.
  • Use it before Angelechy Opposition or Strategy Score. Their lock allows only Synchros, and these are Fusions.
  • Under Simoon's or Vata's DARK lock, Garura and Starving Venom are still legal. Mudragon (WATER) is not.
  • You can also Set it and activate it on your opponent's turn, in the middle of their combo.

  • Angelechy needs no Normal Summon and its effects sit in the Spell & Trap Zone, away from monster removal.
  • Assault Dragon and Destrier both punish every activation with damage.
  • Three Super Polymerization and eleven hand traps.

  • Simoon needs an empty field and a spare Blackwing; Problem needs a Spell/Trap to discard.
  • The deck damages itself: several effects cost 700 to 1000 LP.
  • Angelechy Opposition hands the opponent a monster.

radiant-typhoon.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Eldam into Fonix (going first)

Going first the opponent has no Spells/Traps, so the Level 3s Summon themselves. Eldam finds Meghala. Vision is activated to add Mystical Space Typhoon, and that activation lets Meghala bring Fonix from the Deck. Eldam and Meghala then Link into Marine Eidolon for a second Typhoon. Both are Set for their turn.

Starting hand: Radiant Typhoon Eldam, Radiant Typhoon Vision · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. They control no Spells/Traps: Special Summon Eldam from your hand. It adds Meghala.
  2. Special Summon Meghala from your hand the same way.
  3. Activate Vision: add Mystical Space Typhoon from your Deck.
  4. A Radiant Typhoon Quick-Play was activated: Meghala Special Summons Fonix from your Deck.
  5. Link Summon Marine Eidolon using Eldam + Meghala. It adds a second Mystical Space Typhoon.
  6. Set both Mystical Space Typhoons. Your Normal Summon is still unused.
  7. Their turn: activate a Typhoon on a Spell/Trap. A Quick-Play was activated, so Fonix shuffles up to 2 of their cards into the Deck.

End board: Fonix (3000 ATK) + Marine Eidolon with two Mystical Space Typhoons Set. On their turn the first Typhoon destroys a Spell/Trap and lets Fonix shuffle 2 more cards away. The second Typhoon is another destroy, and it would bring Fonix back from the GY if they had removed it.

  • After Meghala's effect you can only Special Summon WIND monsters this turn. Marine Eidolon is WIND, so it is allowed.
  • Swen starts the same way: it adds Vision or Chant.
  • With Varuroon in hand, it Summons itself when Vision is activated and negates a monster effect once a Typhoon is in your GY.
Line B — Angelechy before the Typhoons

The Angelechy package, played first because Meghala would lock it out. Problem Summons Enlisted and places Destrier, which finds Opposition. Opposition gives the opponent an Enlisted and places Bastion. Your Enlisted banishes theirs, and when it returns to the Extra Deck it brings out a second Destrier as a monster.

Starting hand: Terraforming, Mystical Space Typhoon · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate Terraforming: add Angelechy Problem and activate it.
  2. Problem's effect: discard Mystical Space Typhoon to Special Summon Enlisted and place Destrier as a Continuous Spell.
  3. Destrier was placed: add Angelechy Opposition.
  4. Activate Opposition: Special Summon your second Enlisted to their field, in a column next to yours, and place Bastion.
  5. Your Enlisted's effect: banish their Enlisted. Yours moves to their field and returns to your Extra Deck.
  6. Enlisted changed control, so you Special Summon your second Destrier from the Extra Deck as a monster.

End board: Destrier (2500 ATK) on the field with Destrier and Bastion as Continuous Spells. Each card or effect they activate costs them 500 LP, and Bastion protects your Angelechy cards from destruction. The discarded Typhoon is in your GY, which turns on the Level 3 Radiant Typhoons.

  • After Opposition you can only Special Summon LIGHT or DARK Synchros from the Extra Deck this turn. Marine Eidolon and the Fusions are blocked.
  • The Radiant Typhoon monsters still Summon from hand and Deck, since Opposition only restricts the Extra Deck.
  • On your next turn the monster Destrier banishes 1 monster in a different column.
Line C — Going second with Fonix

Your removal Spells are Quick-Plays, so the first one brings Fonix out of your hand. The Fallen & The Virtuous destroys a card. Mystical Space Typhoon destroys a Spell/Trap, and that second Quick-Play lets Fonix shuffle two more cards into the Deck. Fallen of Albaz then uses one of their remaining monsters as Fusion Material.

Starting hand: The Fallen & The Virtuous, Radiant Typhoon Fonix, the Great Flame, Mystical Space Typhoon, Fallen of Albaz, Forbidden Droplet · Normal Summon: Fallen of Albaz

  1. Activate The Fallen & The Virtuous: send Titaniklad from your Extra Deck to the GY and destroy 1 face-up card.
  2. A Quick-Play was activated: Special Summon Fonix from your hand.
  3. Activate Mystical Space Typhoon: destroy 1 Spell/Trap. Fonix shuffles up to 2 of their cards into the Deck.
  4. Normal Summon Fallen of Albaz. Discard 1 card to fuse Albaz with one of their monsters.
  5. Attack with Fonix (3000) and your Fusion Monster.

End board: Up to five of their cards removed: one destroyed, one Spell/Trap destroyed, two shuffled away and one used as Fusion Material. Fonix and a Level 8 Fusion attack what is left.

  • Albaz + an Extra Deck monster makes Mirrorjade. Albaz + another DARK monster makes Starving Venom.
  • Fonix's Summon and its shuffle are separate effects, each once per turn, so it takes two Quick-Plays to get both.
  • Forbidden Droplet is also a Quick-Play. Use it instead of the Typhoon if a monster is the problem.

  • The Level 3s are free Summons that search, so the Normal Summon is spare.
  • Removal that shuffles, banishes or fuses, which gets around most protection.
  • Mystical Space Typhoon lets the Radiant Typhoon Spells and monsters come back.

  • Quick-Plays must be Set a turn ahead to be used on the opponent's turn.
  • Chant is Limited to 1 and there is only 1 Albaz.

lunalight.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Gold Leo into Liger Dancer

Liger Dancer normally needs four Fusions in a row. Kaleido Chick replaces three of them: she sends Leo Dancer from the Extra Deck to the GY and counts as Leo Dancer herself. Gold Leo finds Silver Hound and discards it, Silver Hound brings Kaleido from the Deck, and Polymerization fuses four Lunalights at once.

Starting hand: Lunalight Gold Leo, Polymerization, Lunalight Black Sheep · Normal Summon: Lunalight Gold Leo

  1. Normal Summon Gold Leo. It adds Silver Hound, then you discard Silver Hound.
  2. Silver Hound was sent to the GY by an effect: Special Summon Kaleido Chick from your Deck. Gold Leo returns Silver Hound to your hand.
  3. Kaleido Chick's effect: send Leo Dancer from your Extra Deck to the GY. Kaleido now counts as Leo Dancer for a Fusion.
  4. Activate Polymerization: Fusion Summon Liger Dancer using Kaleido (as Leo Dancer) + Gold Leo + Silver Hound + Black Sheep.
  5. Kaleido Chick returns Polymerization to your hand. Black Sheep, used as material, adds Gold Leo from your GY.

End board: Liger Dancer (3800 ATK), unaffected by every card that isn't a Lunalight, with Polymerization and Gold Leo back in hand. On either turn it sends a Lunalight from your Extra Deck to destroy all their Special Summoned monsters. Silver Hound in the GY can banish itself and Leo Dancer to negate a Spell or Trap.

  • Each Lunalight effect is once per turn by name. The Silver Hound that returned to your hand can't Summon from the Deck again this turn.
  • While Kaleido Chick is face-up, only Lunalight monsters can come from the Extra Deck. Liger Dancer is one.
  • No third Lunalight in hand? Make Leo Dancer instead (Line B).
Line B — Gold Leo + Black Sheep into Leo Dancer

The two-card version. It starts the same way, then Black Sheep discards itself to fetch Polymerization from the Deck. Kaleido Chick sends Panther Dancer this time, so the Fusion is Leo Dancer and needs only three materials.

Starting hand: Lunalight Gold Leo, Lunalight Black Sheep · Normal Summon: Lunalight Gold Leo

  1. Normal Summon Gold Leo. It adds Silver Hound, then you discard Silver Hound.
  2. Silver Hound Special Summons Kaleido Chick from your Deck. Gold Leo returns Silver Hound to your hand.
  3. Discard Black Sheep: add Polymerization from your Deck.
  4. Kaleido Chick's effect: send Panther Dancer from your Extra Deck to the GY. Kaleido counts as Panther Dancer.
  5. Activate Polymerization: Fusion Summon Leo Dancer using Kaleido (as Panther Dancer) + Gold Leo + Silver Hound.
  6. Kaleido Chick was sent to the GY by an effect: return Polymerization to your hand.

End board: Leo Dancer (3500 ATK) with Polymerization in hand. They can't target it or destroy it with card effects. It attacks twice, and after it attacks a monster it destroys every Special Summoned monster they control. Silver Hound and Panther Dancer in the GY are a Spell/Trap negate.

  • Fire Formation - Tenki adds Gold Leo, so Tenki + Black Sheep is the same line.
  • Black Sheep discarded for its own effect is a cost, so it doesn't trigger. That is fine here: you only want the Polymerization.
  • Going second, attack a monster with Leo Dancer first, clear their field with its effect, then make the second attack directly.
Line C — Fraktall start

For hands without Gold Leo. Fraktall sends Silver Hound from the Deck to the GY, and Silver Hound Summons Gold Leo from the Deck. Gold Leo adds Kaleido Chick, which you Normal Summon. Black Sheep fetches Polymerization and Gold Leo takes Black Sheep straight back, so it is still there as the third material.

Starting hand: Tri-Brigade Fraktall, Lunalight Black Sheep, Effect Veiler · Normal Summon: Lunalight Kaleido Chick

  1. Send Fraktall from your hand to the GY: send Silver Hound from your Deck to the GY.
  2. Silver Hound Special Summons Gold Leo from your Deck. Gold Leo adds Kaleido Chick, then you discard 1 card (here Effect Veiler).
  3. Normal Summon Kaleido Chick and send Panther Dancer from your Extra Deck to the GY.
  4. Discard Black Sheep: add Polymerization. Gold Leo returns Black Sheep from the GY to your hand.
  5. Activate Polymerization: Fusion Summon Leo Dancer using Kaleido (as Panther Dancer) + Gold Leo + Black Sheep.
  6. Kaleido returns Polymerization. Black Sheep, used as material, adds Gold Leo from your GY.

End board: Leo Dancer (3500 ATK) with Polymerization and Gold Leo in hand for next turn. Silver Hound and Panther Dancer in the GY give you the Spell/Trap negate.

  • Foolish Burial (send Silver Hound) starts this line the same way.
  • Foolish Burial Goods sends Serenade Dance: banish it and send a card from your hand to Summon Gold Leo from the Deck.
  • Use only Fraktall's first effect. Its second effect needs a Link Monster the deck doesn't run.
lunalight.str:
• Two cards make Leo Dancer, three make Liger Dancer, on the first turn.
  • Leo and Liger Dancer clear every Special Summoned monster and attack twice.
  • Polymerization keeps coming back through Kaleido Chick and Masquerade.
  • Silver Hound in the GY is a free Spell/Trap negate.

spright.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Starter into the Spright board

Two cards, no Normal Summon. Starter brings Jet from the Deck, and Jet finds Smashers. Blue Summons itself because a Level 2 is on the field, and finds Red, which does the same. Jet + Blue overlay into Gigantic Spright, and Gigantic detaches a material to bring Carrot from the Deck.

Starting hand: Spright Starter, Spright Blue · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate Spright Starter: Special Summon Jet from your Deck (you lose 1300 LP). Jet adds Spright Smashers.
  2. You control a Level 2: Special Summon Blue from your hand. Blue adds Spright Red.
  3. Special Summon Red from your hand the same way.
  4. Xyz Summon Gigantic Spright (Rank 2) using Jet + Blue.
  5. Gigantic's effect: detach 1 material to Special Summon Carrot from your Deck.
  6. Set Spright Smashers. You still have your Normal Summon.

End board: Gigantic Spright + Red + Carrot with Smashers Set. Red Tributes Gigantic to negate a monster effect and destroy that monster. Carrot Tributes another 2 to negate a Spell or Trap. Smashers banishes a Spright from your GY, then one of your 2s and one of their cards.

  • No Starter? Normal Summon any Spright, then Special Summon Jet and Blue next to it for their searches.
  • After Starter you can only Special Summon Level, Rank or Link 2 monsters this turn.
  • Each Spright can Summon itself from hand once per turn, and each search is once per turn.
Line B — Nadir Servant and Dogmatika (going second)

Nadir Servant sends a monster from your Extra Deck to the GY and adds a Dogmatika monster with ATK equal to or lower than it. Send Elder Entity N'tss: it destroys a card, and its 2500 ATK finds Fleurdelis. Their Extra Deck monsters let Ecclesia and Fleurdelis Summon themselves, and Fleurdelis negates a monster.

Starting hand: Nadir Servant, Dogmatika Ecclesia, the Virtuous · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate Nadir Servant: send Elder Entity N'tss from your Extra Deck to the GY and add Fleurdelis.
  2. N'tss was sent to the GY: destroy 1 card on the field.
  3. An Extra Deck monster is on the field: Special Summon Ecclesia from your hand.
  4. Fleurdelis's Quick Effect: Special Summon it from your hand, then negate 1 face-up monster until the end of the turn.
  5. When a Dogmatika attacks, Fleurdelis gives all your Dogmatika monsters 500 ATK: Fleurdelis 3000, Ecclesia 2000.

End board: One card destroyed, their best monster negated, and 5000 ATK of Dogmatika monsters attacking. Ecclesia can't be destroyed in battle by monsters from the Extra Deck.

  • Sending Garura instead draws 1 card and adds Ecclesia (1500 ATK), who then searches Fleurdelis.
  • After Nadir Servant you can't Special Summon from the Extra Deck this turn. Sprights from hand and Deck are still fine.
  • Ecclesia and Fleurdelis need a monster that was Special Summoned from the Extra Deck on the field, either player's.
Line C — Evenly Matched, then Sprights

The standard going-second turn. Evenly Matched can be activated from your hand if you control no cards, at the end of the Battle Phase. So you play nothing in Main Phase 1, walk into the Battle Phase, and make them banish their field down to one card. Then you build Line A in Main Phase 2.

Starting hand: Evenly Matched, Spright Starter, Spright Blue · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Main Phase 1: play nothing, so that you control no cards. Go to the Battle Phase.
  2. End of the Battle Phase: activate Evenly Matched from your hand. They banish cards face-down until they control 1.
  3. Main Phase 2: activate Spright Starter and Special Summon Jet from your Deck.
  4. Play the rest of Line A: Blue, Red, Gigantic Spright, Carrot.

End board: They are down to one card, banished face-down so that nothing triggers, and they face Gigantic Spright, Red and Carrot.

  • Your opponent chooses which card to keep.
  • Evenly Matched is a Trap activated from the hand: Ash Blossom can't stop it, but a Counter Trap or a Spell/Trap negate can.
  • Nibiru is the alternative on their turn: once they have Summoned 5 monsters, it Tributes their whole field.
Going second — Super Polymerization

Super Polymerization is a Quick-Play Spell: discard 1 card, then Fusion Summon using monsters from either field. Neither player can respond to it. Two of their best monsters (or one of theirs and one of yours) become one Fusion Monster on your side. The materials are sent to the GY without being targeted or destroyed, so their protection doesn't help. Pick the Fusion by what the two monsters share:

  • Same Type and same Attribute: Garura, Wings of Resonant Life. Any 2 monsters with different names. Garura doubles the battle damage it deals and draws you 1 card when it goes to the GY. Your own pair: Spright Blue + Spright Jet (DARK Thunder).
  • Same Attribute, different Types: Mudragon of the Swamp. Your opponent can't target Mudragon, or any monster sharing its Attribute, with card effects. Your own pair: Spright Red (Thunder) + Ash Blossom (Zombie), both FIRE.
  • Two DARK monsters (no Tokens): Starving Venom Fusion Dragon. Gains the ATK of one of their Special Summoned monsters this turn, and can copy the name and effects of a Level 5+ monster they control. Your own: Blue, Jet and Gigantic Spright are DARK.
  • Use it before Spright Starter or Gigantic Spright's effect. Their lock allows only Level/Rank/Link 2 Special Summons, and none of these Fusions is Level 2.
  • Also use it before Nadir Servant, which stops Extra Deck Summons for the turn.
  • You can also Set it and activate it on your opponent's turn, in the middle of their combo.
spright.str:
• Spright Starter is a one-card route to the full board.
  • Red, Carrot and Smashers give three different answers on the opponent's turn.
  • Nineteen hand traps and breakers: the strongest going-second package in the collection.
  • Dogmatika gets removal and card draw out of Extra Deck cards you would never Summon.
spright.weak:
• Without Starter you need two Sprights or a Normal Summon to begin.
  • The Starter, Gigantic and Dogmatika locks all restrict the same turn.
  • Low ATK: the board wins by negating, not by fighting.
  • Starter's LP cost adds up over a long game.

gren-maju.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Plan A — Turn-one lock

The control opening. Pot of Duality finds whichever piece is missing. Inspector Boarder is Normal Summoned onto an empty field, a floodgate Spell goes face-up, and Macro Cosmos is Set with a Solemn Trap beside it. Nothing here needs a Special Summon, so Duality's restriction costs nothing.

Starting hand: Pot of Duality, Inspector Boarder, Necrovalley, Macro Cosmos, Solemn Judgment · Normal Summon: Inspector Boarder

  1. Activate Pot of Duality: reveal your top 3 cards and add 1 to your hand.
  2. Normal Summon Inspector Boarder while you control no monsters.
  3. Activate Necrovalley in your Field Zone.
  4. Set Macro Cosmos and Solemn Judgment.
  5. Their turn: flip Macro Cosmos as soon as you can. Use Solemn Judgment on the card that would break the lock.

End board: Inspector Boarder + Necrovalley + Macro Cosmos, backed by Solemn Judgment. With no Extra Deck monster on the field they can activate no monster effects at all. Their GY is frozen, and every card they lose from now on is banished.

  • Dimensional Fissure does Macro Cosmos's job for monsters and doesn't have to wait a turn.
  • Don't Set Infinite Impermanence in the same column as your face-up Continuous Spells. If it was Set, it negates other Spell/Trap effects in its column for the turn.
  • Solemn Judgment costs half your LP. Save it for a Feather Duster or a boss monster.
Plan B — Gren Maju for game

The attacking turn. Raigeki clears their monsters. Pot of Desires banishes 10 cards from your Deck and Gizmek Orochi banishes 8 more to Summon itself, so Gren Maju arrives with 18 × 400 ATK. Clockwork Night adds 500 to both of your monsters.

Starting hand: Raigeki, Pot of Desires, Gizmek Orochi, the Serpentron Sky Slasher, Gren Maju Da Eiza, Clockwork Night · Normal Summon: Gren Maju Da Eiza

  1. Activate Raigeki: destroy all monsters they control.
  2. Activate Pot of Desires: banish the top 10 cards of your Deck face-down and draw 2.
  3. Gizmek Orochi's Quick Effect: banish the top 8 cards of your Deck to Special Summon it from your hand.
  4. Normal Summon Gren Maju Da Eiza. You have 18 banished cards, so it has 7200 ATK.
  5. Activate Clockwork Night: your monsters gain 500 ATK. Gren Maju is 7700 and Orochi is 2950.
  6. Attack directly with both for 10,650 damage.

End board: A win from 8000 LP in one Battle Phase. Even without Raigeki, a 7700 ATK attacker destroys almost anything, and each further banished card adds 400.

  • Do this on a turn when Inspector Boarder is not on your field: it would stop Orochi's Summon.
  • Don't play Pot of Prosperity in the same turn as Pot of Desires. Prosperity stops you drawing with card effects.
  • With Macro Cosmos or Dimensional Fissure out, Gren Maju also grows with every card you lose.
Plan C — Albaz takes their monster

Fallen of Albaz, when Normal Summoned, fuses itself with a monster your opponent controls. Their monster is used as material, so its protection doesn't matter. Mirrorjade then banishes a second monster. Decisive Battle of Golgonda keeps the Fusion alive by sending another Albaz Fusion from the Extra Deck in its place.

Starting hand: Fallen of Albaz, Decisive Battle of Golgonda, Necrovalley · Normal Summon: Fallen of Albaz

  1. Activate Decisive Battle of Golgonda.
  2. Normal Summon Fallen of Albaz. Discard 1 card to fuse Albaz with their Extra Deck monster into Mirrorjade.
  3. Mirrorjade's Quick Effect: send Titaniklad from your Extra Deck to the GY and banish 1 monster.
  4. If Mirrorjade would be destroyed, Golgonda sends Brigrand from your Extra Deck to the GY instead.

End board: Mirrorjade (3000 ATK) protected by Golgonda once per turn, with two of their monsters gone. If they do remove Mirrorjade with a card effect, it destroys all their monsters in the End Phase.

  • This needs monster effects, so don't have Inspector Boarder on the field first.
  • There is only 1 Albaz. Titaniklad's and Brigrand's End Phase searches find it only if it is still in the Deck.
  • The next slide lists which Fusion each kind of monster makes.
Going second — Which Fusion to make

Fallen of Albaz fuses with a monster they control (discard 1). Super Polymerization fuses any two monsters on either field and can't be responded to. Either way their monsters are used as material, not targeted or destroyed. Choose by what their monsters are:

  • Albaz + a Fusion, Synchro, Xyz or Link: Mirrorjade the Iceblade Dragon. Then Mirrorjade banishes another monster as a Quick Effect.
  • Albaz + a Level 8+ monster, or one with 2500+ ATK: Brigrand the Glory Dragon, Titaniklad the Ash Dragon. Brigrand can't be destroyed by battle. Titaniklad gains ATK from both Levels.
  • Albaz + a Fusion Monster: Predaplant Dragostapelia. Dragostapelia puts a counter on a monster each turn and negates that monster's effects.
  • Two DARK monsters: Starving Venom Fusion Dragon. Starving Venom. Also Albaz + any DARK monster.
  • Same Type and Attribute, or same Attribute only: Garura, Wings of Resonant Life, Mudragon of the Swamp. Garura draws when it leaves. Mudragon protects against targeting.
  • Their Link Monsters: Earth Golem @Ignister, World Chalice Guardragon Almarduke. Earth Golem needs a Cyberse + a Link. Almarduke needs three Links, and attacks every monster.
  • Check Types and Attributes before you activate. You choose the Fusion as Super Polymerization resolves.
  • Pot of Duality and Card of Demise stop Special Summons for the turn, Fusions included.
  • Albaz + a Dragon makes Alba-Lenatus, which can take several of their Dragons at once.
gren-maju.str:
• Floodgates that attack the GY, monster effects, Types and big monsters at once.
  • Gren Maju reaches 7000+ ATK from two cards and can't be stopped by your own lock.
  • The interaction is Traps, which work under Inspector Boarder.
  • Super Polymerization and Albaz remove monsters without targeting or destroying.
gren-maju.weak:
• The floodgates restrict you too, so sequencing mistakes cost the game.
  • Only ten monsters, and three of them do nothing until cards are banished.
  • Spell/Trap removal such as Harpie's Feather Duster undoes the whole lock.
  • Pot of Desires and Orochi can run you out of Deck.
